It.StringStory.302030055: Jung Yerim's mother was a crook, and even as a young high school student, Yerim was expected to help with her schemes. In the end, her mother's greed destroyed their lives. As she watched her mother being led away in handcuffs, Jung Yerim shed no tears. Meanwhile, the person they had scammed the most, Park Jongsoo, the guild master of the Knights Guild, reached out to help her, calling himself "Daddy Long Legs." Jung Yerim wanted to repay his kindness. In her short life, he was the only light she had ever known, the one person who taught her what a true adult looked like. To save him, she awakened all the light she possessed. That was how Jung Yerim became the primary healer of the Knights Guild. With her innate talents as a healer and meticulous money-management skills, Jung Yerim started repaying her debt. Treasuring the brooch over her heart, she closes the books on another flawless calculation. "Kindness or salvation, everything comes with a price. Mine is no exception."

She noticed even the slightest of changes in the environment, and nearly every time she thought something bad was going to happen, it did.

It.StringStory.302030054:
In the depths where Sung Jinwoo's consciousness had sunk lay everything he had ever longed for: his mother healthy, his stolen time returned, and a world untouched by battle or death.

Yet the emptiness in his heart remained unfilled.

From the darkness emerged Ashborn, the Former Monarch of Shadows clad in jet-black armor. Bearing the crushing weight of death, the Shadow spoke.

"I am the history of your struggle, and the reward for your suffering. I am you."

An eternity of peaceful rest, or a battlefield of ruin. Sung Jinwoo didn't hesitate. The world hadn't yet reached its end.

The moment Ashborn vanished into the World of Nothingness, his once-buried powers of death were unleashed.

Reborn as the true Monarch of Shadows, Jinwoo gave his first command to the darkness that awaited him.

"Arise."

A Shadow's judgement is a blade of pitch-black steel, etched with the resolve of one who chose the battlefield instead of eternal peace.

At the 5th Advancement, <color=#64FAC8>[Mark of the Oath, Sanctuary's Blessing, and Unwavering Oath]</color> gain enhanced effects while <color=#64FAC8>[Holy Bond]</color>, which is activated by using her <color=#FAC800>Ultimate Skill</color>, is active. It.StringStory.302030053:
To Agnes Rivera, family was something chosen, not something bound by blood. Even to the gambler's son taken in as payment for a debt, she offered her hand without hesitation. Her family gave him food, taught him how to read, and showed him how to survive. To Agnes, it only made sense.

That was what it meant to become family.

But on the night of her birthday, Dante Grossi appeared beyond the locked doors of his old pharmacy, staring at her with the eyes of a traitor.

"Not once, in all the time I stood beside you, did I ever love you. I devoted my entire life to hating you, Agnes Rivera."

As the blade pierced his neck, Agnes kept her hand locked in place until the very moment his breathing stopped.

Only then did she realize what hell her family had put him through behind her back.

With her weapons resting in her grip, Agnes made a vow. She would always sees things through with her own hands, for the things she lost and the things she refused to lose.

"La famiglia. To protect my family."

With the names of those she's lost etched into every round, she pulls the trigger.

It.StringStory.302030052:
From a young age, Liu Zhigang had always illuminated the lives of everyone around him. With the weight of his family's name behind him, he believed that one day he would be able to share his light with everyone.

But when he awakened as a hunter, he found that his closest friend was on a road where he could not follow. His swordmaster's voice lingered in his ears as he left home the following dawn.

"Don't lose your sense of right and wrong. Your very name is the true blade you wield."

When the Kamish raid had come and gone, the unforgettable image of the battlefield in his mind was overlayed with the names of every fallen friend he couldn't bring home. So he fled. The unhonored trust in their eyes weighed on him heavily.

But his remaining comrades continued searching for him until he was forced to look them in the eye, and only then did Liu Zhigang finally lower his head and beg forgiveness. And by the time he returned to the world he had left behind, his friend was already gone.

In the cold, silent dawn, he gripped two swords in his hands.

"The dawn you once championed... I will bring it fourth."

Though he once saw his light die, the coming day cuts through the darkened skies.

It.StringStory.302030051:
Myro O'Dwyer was beloved by all. She lived a life far removed from conflict, worry, despair, or sorrow. Beneath glittering chandeliers, she earned endless admiration as her fingers flew across the piano keys.

She was a seemingly eternal princess of the ivories, and never once had she questioned her own status.

How foolish and naive her thoughts had been. In an instant, she was dragged from the world she knew. Her glamorous world, her family, and even the admiration she had earned with her own two hands turned into condemnation.

She wouldn't even be given a choice in how she would die. So she refused to give in. The moment she flicked on the lighter, she let out a sound that was something between laughter and tears.

Her world burned brightly. And beneath the radiant white flames, a presence emerged, whispering a tempting offer in a chilling voice.

"Successor of the White Flames, prove yourself worthy by burning away your former life."

Now, the White Flames granted by the lord of the Demons' Castle rested in her slender hands. Her fury burned with elegance and precision, yet also with savage brutality.

"Gladly, my lord."

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc078:
Jinwoo saw his father.

He was staring at Jinwoo from inside the gate of the amusement park. Jinwoo wasn't sure if he should be happy or resentful. The situation was too strange. Sung Jinwoo thought for a while before finally speaking.

"It's been a while."

There were so many things he wanted to say when his father returned, but seeing him face to face like this, all he could do was greet him. His father continued to stare at Sung Jinwoo and then squeezed his hand tightly as he shouted something.

Strangely, he couldn't hear his father's voice, but he could feel his father's strength when he held his hand. Sung Jinwoo read his father's lips as he shouted with all his might, and as soon as he understood the word, "heart," light poured from behind his father's back and Sung Jinwoo opened his eyes.

Before becoming a hunter, his life wasn't really saint-like. Like most people, happiness and hardship coexisted.

His strength wasn't built for protection, but to overpower his rivals. Perhaps that's why his new power became the opposite: one that shone brilliantly as a power of healing.

"But at this point..."

His healing abilities were both powerful and radiant, yet they couldn't bring back the one person Antoine wished he could heal. Antoine fell into despair, but he had no time to remain broken.

There was far too much suffering in the world, and his angel had seen him as a hero.

"Angela, I'll save them all, just as you would have wanted."

It was only after losing the one little girl he had sworn to protect that he was reborn as a true saint.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc001:
The appearance of mana brought new opportunities for some and despair for others.

For Cha Hae-In, it was both. Her awakening was a once-in-a-lifetime event that brought her both joy and pain.

She had been a promising track and field athlete, on her way to amazing things.

She had a pretty good track record, but even people who weren't interested in track and field knew her name because a video of her competing went viral.

She was more interested in pushing her personal bests than fame, but the public wanted a new star and showered her with attention.

As a young athlete who didn't enjoy being in the limelight, she was embarrassed by this kind of attention.

However, the people around her tried to take advantage of it. People's interest in certain athletic sports can rely heavily on the fame of specific competitors, after all.

While the adults around her pressured her to embrace her newfound fame, she shied away from the cameras and kept to herself, focusing on becoming a better athlete.

What she learned is that attention doesn't make you better at something- and the pressure that comes with it can do the opposite.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc003:
At the end of middle school, Cha Hae-In participated in the first round of the national student track and field competition. She injured her ankle during the race, but instead of quitting, she decided to press on.

She was able to finish, but just barely. To make things worse, she had strained her ankle so badly, she was forced to spend more than a year recovering from her injury.

In a way, Cha Hae-In got what she wanted: her fame dissipated as achievements failed materialize.

But so did her career as an athlete. She retired from competing shortly after that.

A cruel fate for someone as passionate as her, all caused by a single mistake.

Cha Hae-In had never wanted anything but to be an athlete. Every day, she regretted the choice she made. "If I was given just one more chance," she thought, "I wouldn't have pushed on and ruined my ankle."

But as she had watched the other runners speed ahead, she couldn't help herself. She felt it from deep down, from her core. She wanted to run. To compete. To not let them win.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc018:
Some believe evil is innate.

Even as a child, Kang Taeshik would delight in tormenting insects and small animals.

He would then respectfully lay them to rest.

He started conducting a ceremony before he began his remorseless torture as well, until this ritual evolved into something he found sacred.

Taeshik was clever enough to never get caught. In front of others, he was a model student and upright citizen.

In mass media, people regularly discussed what might go through the head of serial killers in movies and TV shows.

He laughed discreetly; none of the fictional depictions seemed realistic to him.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc002:
Contrary to her wishes, the public remained interested in her for quite a long time. Cha Hae-In was really uncomfortable being a household name, but fate had other plans.

She was walking on eggshells knowing that every one of her words and actions was examined, as if under a microscope. People even spread lies about her.

Even her greatest achievements were stained by the words of anonymous anti-fans.

But Cha Hae-In remained strong.

Her love of running and passion for honest competition kept her going.

Her drive, however, led her to her downfall.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc074:
Lee Bora started doing her own research to explain everything "paranormal" with cold, hard facts.

Only when she found the explanation for something odd and confirmed that it matched to the tiniest detail, she felt her anxieties ease a little. Her grandmother had insisted that Bora walk the same path as her. She was comforted that each explanation loosened her grandmother's vice grip on her future.

But the world had something else in store for her, as the supernatural soon invaded every aspect of human life. And as salt in the wound, the world made her one of the people that could use these supernatural powers.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc019:
There wasn't some tragic origin story behind Taeshik's merciless behavior.

It was just his kind of fun. He loved watching his victims struggle to avoid imminent death, and he enjoyed hearing cries of terror.

He eventually got tired of inflicting the same kind of pain again and again and started to look for new and more exciting endeavors.

A life without excitement was boring.

He needed something even more stimulating.

And the ultimate stimulation was always the most dangerous prey: humans.

He started looking for his first victim. And finally, he decided on a target.
Story.CharacterInfo_Desc005:
Cha Hae-In slowly opened her eyes, crouched down, and corrected her stance. For some odd reason, she felt that she could pull off the perfect run now.

Mysterious energy was pumping through her arms, legs, and deep down within her heart. She knew instinctively that she could run again- maybe even better than before.

She left all of her worries behind and sprinted into the evening breeze. When she looked back, she noticed that her feet had left deep dents in the ground.

It was a sign. Though she could no longer be the athlete that she wanted to be, she was about to start competing on a whole new level.

She might've wrapped her head around it if she was given the ability to strengthen her body to make some sort of physical attack, but the power she was given was a force beyond our current understanding of physics

Even though she'd lived her life determined to see the world as it was, she was doomed to see the same illusions as her grandmother.

But if her destiny were unavoidable, then she'd better stop wallowing about it.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc069:
Hwang Dongsoo was the eighth S-Rank hunter born in South Korea, but he belongs to the Scavenger Guild in America.

He has been widely criticized for "forsaking his country," but he seemingly doesn't care. On the day he left for America, a crowd and reporters gathered at the airport and asked why he was going. Following a suffocating silence, Hwang Dongsoo answered, "Since I became an S-Rank hunter, I haven't gotten anything from the Hunters Association except their rancid breath on my neck."

However, the Hunters Association had reasons to keep a close watch on the S-Rank hunter, who was considered an important national resource.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc004:
But that feeling was all she was left with.

As a result of her injury, she could no longer run like she used to. She grew resentful as her legs didn't move like she wanted, and eventually stopped believing that she could regain what she had lost.

However, her competitive spirit never completely faded, and eventually led her down a new track.

Standing at the edge of an empty field, she closed her eyes, recalling the times when she was able to run to her heart's content.

In the following silence, she could only feel her ears, her eyes, and her legs.

At the sound of the signal, her legs sped her toward the goal line.

Only when she finally reached it could she hear the world around her again. Even if it was all in her head, she felt satisfied.

Lee Bora had considered pretending that she didn't have the ability to feel mana and living out the rest of her life as a regular person.

Instead, she would rather run headfirst into the world of mana and the power she'd been given. Through first-hand experience, and lots and lots of data, she could then arrive at a new truth... Maybe she could have kept her belief.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc007:
After trying out different sports, he chose to pursue track and field. After all, there was no sport better suited to pushing the raw physical limits of the human body. And as expected, he rocketed to the top.

During his races, he would often look back at the "losers" behind him and think to himself:

"There's a clear and unmistakable gap in talent.

They're all morons to keep competing against someone with such an overwhelming advantage."

Basking in his "God-given talent," Chul quit track and field shortly afterwards, satisfied with his dominating performance. He needed a greater challenge. One that would garner him even more praise and recognition.

When his older brother discovered a "new way of making money" that could only be done with his powers and cut him out of the deal, Dongsoo was furious. He followed his older brother, despite knowing that only awakened beings can safely enter a dungeon.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc006:
Kim Chul never failed.

He was naturally fast and strong. He was a born athlete. Before he became a hunter, he had tried many sports, but quickly lost interest in every one.

The reason was simple.

It was all too easy. Though he never played a sport for long, it was long enough for him to gauge his own talent and potential.

He was constantly told, "If you take on the right training regimen, you're going to make a name for yourself." That was all he needed to hear. He decided that it was inevitable: he was going to be an athletic star.
Story.CharacterInfo_Desc070:
Hwang Dongsoo and his older brother Hwang Dongsuk had extensive criminal records for violence and theft.

Of course, awakening as a hunter isn't reserved only for the pure of heart... but it's cause for concern when a pair of hooligans awaken as S-Rank! When people with extensive criminal records gain unparalleled powers, there's the risk that they'll use their gifts for personal gain instead of closing gates.

Upset by the Hunters Association's suspicions, Dongsoo had no hesitations about moving to the USA.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc066:
Dongsoo had always been in his brother's shadow. Dongsuk was the only one that ever received praise.

Even when their parents' death started to lead Dongsuk down a dangerous path, Dongsoo couldn't escape the need to outdo him.

Wanting to be better than his brother drove him to commit acts of worse and worse nature. After all, the two brothers considered their rap sheets a list of achievements.

Even when the gates appeared and the power of mana changed the balance of the world, Dongsoo couldn't beat Dongsuk.

Dongsoo congratulated his brother when he awakened as a C-Rank, but boiled with jealousy.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc094:
Hunters have a saying: What happens in the dungeon stays in the dungeon.

All kinds of dangers lurk in dungeons, and the rules of the outside world don't apply. A dungeon is an excellent scene for a crime, and a crime committed in a dungeon more than likely goes unsolved.

There was one incident, though, which got the world's attention. The Hunters Association called in on a raid on a D-Rank dungeon, and there, a criminal went on a killing spree! He was only arrested thanks to the combined efforts of the surviving hunters, including Park Beom-Shik and Kim Sangshik.

This incident led to the creation of laws related to gates, dungeons, and hunters' crimes, but these were difficult to enforce.

Dungeons were still dangerous, and many Hunters quit the business due to their dissatisfaction that their safety could not be guaranteed.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc071:
When Hwang Dongsoo left for the States, he asked his brother to come with him, but Hwang Dongsuk declined.

At least, that's how the story goes. Since the two brothers always worked together, people were surprised by Hwang Dongsuk's choice. They shouldn't have been, though - though they seemed like a perfect sibling team to outsiders, the pair held no loyalty to each other.

Dongsoo had always been in his brother's shadow. Dongsuk was the only one that ever received praise.

Even when their parents' deaths started to lead Dongsuk down a dangerous path, Dongsoo couldn't escape the need to outdo him.

Wanting to be better than his brother drove him to become worse and worse. After all, the two brothers considered their rap sheets a list of achievements.
Story.CharacterInfo_Desc065:
Dongsoo and Dongsuk had extensive criminal records for violence and theft. And since they had gained powers, ordinary humans were no match for them. The Association suspected that instead of using their gifts for killing monsters, they were using their powers for crime.

Upset with the Hunters Association's accusations, Dongsoo had no qualms about moving to the USA.

When he left for the States, he asked his brother to come with him, but Hwang Dongsuk declined. At least, that's how the story goes.

The two brothers seemed to have a strong bond. Since they had always worked together, people were surprised by Hwang Dongsuk's decision.

Though their brotherly bond looked perfect on the outside, on the inside, there was no loyalty.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc095:
Park Beom-Shik and Kim Sangshik, though they had survived the same incident, set off on different paths. They both prioritized their families, but Park Beom-Shik wanted a peaceful life, and Kim Sangshik wanted his family to be stable.

After quitting his job as a hunter, Park Beom-Shik tried to find a "normal and safe" job like his wife wanted, but it wasn't easy. None of the jobs he was qualified to do could come close to the income he'd earned as a hunter.

He was used to having high standards, and the idea of working for peanuts left him cold. He had plenty of savings, so he decided to take a long and well-earned vacation. The problem could wait!

But it could not wait for long. His wife was pregnant with their second child, and the hard-fought balance of his bank account was running low.

Park Beom-Shik had no choice. He decided to go back to being a hunter, something he'd sworn to never do. Since he was breaking his promise, he decided to make it count and chase a big payday.

Unfortunately, what was meant to be his comeback turned out to be his final battle.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc072:
Even when the gates appeared and the power of mana changed the balance of the world, Dongsoo couldn't beat Dongsuk. Hwang Dongsuk was declared an Awakened Being a little earlier than Hwang Dongsoo. Dongsoo congratulated his brother when he awakened as a C-Rank, but boiled with jealousy. When his older brother discovered a "new way of making money" that could only be done with his powers and cut Dongsoo out of the deal, Dongsoo was furious. He followed his older brother, despite knowing that only awakened beings could safely enter a dungeon.

He survived - and realized that he had powers as well.

On the day he was evaluated as an S-Rank, with mana beyond what machines could measure, he clenched his fists with joy. For the first time in his life, he had surpassed Dongsuk.
Story.CharacterInfo_Desc064:
He studied hard so he could work for the Hunters Association.

Unfortunately for him, his awakening made most of his efforts to understand the business aspects worthless, but he wasn't too bothered. He wanted to be in the field as much as possible, anyhow.

Finally, the day came. He stood in front of Go Gunhee as a new employee and told him about his dream, confident that it was the first step to making it a reality.

But dreams never really come true.

Only shortly after achieving his goal of joining the Hunters Association, Woo Jinchul received a harsh dose of reality.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc092:
Anna evolved abilities.

Whenever she drew a bow, the arrow became poisoned - a useful skill which the prison saw fit to lend out.

Day in and day out, she fought for her life inside Gates, and before she knew it, her sentence was up.

Though she had her freedom, there were few opportunities available to her, except to use her ability, and so she worked alone for a period of time.

Then one day, a Dungeon Break alarm sounded, calling any capable hunters to report right away.

Anna had never fought in a Dungeon Break before, but, curious, she ran to the source of the danger.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc073:
Nothing in the world is unexplainable. That's what Lee Bora always thought.

The supernatural is but a myth, created by humans to explain things beyond their comprehension. Even if something inexplicable were to happen in front of her very eyes, she believed that it was only her lack of immediate understanding that left her without an explanation and that with time and knowledge, she'd be able to fully understand what had happened.

There was no time to waste on being bewildered by illusions or chasing phantoms. If you let even one ethereal problem into your life, it wouldn't be long before they took over. She arrived at this conclusion when she was just a little girl, after seeing the twisted look on her grandmother's face as she talked about the incorporeal.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc093:
The monsters flooding outwards from a Dungeon Break had surrounded the fast food restaurant where Anna's life had changed.

Civilians were screaming and scrambling in fear, and some already lay dead. Many hunters were on the scene, but it seemed like their powers weren't enough.

Then, a loud noise emerged from the depths of the restaurant.

Anna saw people shaking with fear as they locked the doors to keep the magic beasts outside out. And inside, she saw terrified familiar faces.

Her former coworkers didn't recognize her. They seemed to believe that Anna was a Hunter who'd come to save them. She could see the hope in their eyes... How shameless of them.

Someone screamed. The magic beasts had breached the door! Anna stood back and watched as they laid waste to the restaurant and the people who'd taken refuge there.

She smiled quietly to herself and felt no pity.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc062:
Woo Jinchul thought about why he wanted to bring the evildoers to justice.

It wasn't because of self-centered ambition or a desire to be seen as a hero - it was because he wanted to protect innocent victims from more harm.

He began to seek out stories of people who'd suffered because of the gates.

And then, during his research, he had a thought: The hunters protect the civilians, but who protects the hunters?

At the time, hunters had begun to form the very first guilds to conquer dungeons together, but there was nothing in the news about services or protections being offered to hunters.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc090:
Honestly, Anna didn't feel sorry for them at all.

She just took the subway and went to work like she normally did.

She kept her head down and minded her own business.

She didn't have any responsibilities outside of flipping burgers.

However, that day, something in the air seemed changed. Her manager, usually an absent boss, was nitpicking her every move, and she felt certain she could hear her coworkers sneering at her, even though they'd never spoken to each other before.

It wasn't long before the police came.

Just like that, Anna was charged with theft and thrown in jail - and she was out of a job.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc061:
The world shown by the news was devastating.

In an amusement park that should be filled with dreams and hope, blood-covered hunters were groaning, and people were screaming and scattering in all directions.

The chaotic noises and the amusement park's cheerful music created an unnatural melody.

The gate was finally closed, and a boy was standing in front of it with unfocused eyes. Just like that, the news ended. It was later known that the boy was the son of a hunter who helped his comrades who were trapped inside the closing gate, and he was the only one who was unable to escape.

Strangely, there were more stories on the news that day about the hunters who joined forces to defeat the magic beasts than about the hunter who had gone missing.

Clearly, someone was sacrificed, and a family lost a precious member that day.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc091:
Anna felt wronged. She had no idea of the charges until the police dragged her away.

More than one true culprit had framed Anna for their crimes.

Because they thought Anna thought she was better than them, they carefully crafted a plan for her downfall.

The crime was bad, but not terrible, so Anna was only sentenced to a few years in jail.

She was worried that the world would change while she was behind bars, but other than that, it was fine. She'd just bide her time until she got out, and then find another job where she could keep to herself.

But, with the appearance of magic beasts, the world changed more quickly than anyone could have imagined.

How long has it been? For Anna, the change in the world meant new opportunities.

It.StringStory.302030036_IDLE2:
Time was short, and the threshold of expectation is unbearably high. Each day felt like she was staring into an hourglass where the sand was gradually falling through.

Then one day, misfortune came knocking. She stood before a dungeon, hardly believing this was really happening.

"If it's for my team, I can be or do anything."

As if lightning had been sparked inside her, her heart started racing. She stepped inside, determined to win.

She was already used to being a leader. She knew she'd have to get even more used to it in the days ahead.

Fear and uncertainty made her knees knock together, but she quickly shook her head and brushed the anxiety aside. This was, in the end, for the people she held dear.

As long as those dear to her stood behind her, she had no intention of retreating.

It.StringStory.302030038_IDLE2:
One day, she started having strange dreams. In them, she saw a beautiful world where a purple butterfly fluttered and flower petals scattered in the air.

Yet, not everything in that world was beautiful. The magic beasts that appeared before her attacked with terrifying screams, and just as she screamed, her vision blurred.

Then, another version of herself appeared as if to take her place and whispered softly.

"Don't think of this as just a passing dream."

She wielded a huge scythe and attacked the magic beasts, moving gracefully, as if dancing.

"Just do it the way you always have. Use your talents and your joy. Don't forget: that's the fastest path out of the dark."

<color=#AF64AF>[Dark]</color> Striker
This hunter cannot recover their MP with their Basic Attack. They must stack the <color=#64FAC8>[Ruler's Upgrade]</color> effect using their <color=#FAC800>Basic Skill</color> and then use their <color=#FAC800>Ultimate Skill</color> to recover their MP. Their <color=#FAC800>Ultimate Skill</color> refreshes the duration of the buff they have increasing their combat stamina. Additionally, their <color=#FAC800>Ultimate Skill</color> inflicts a special status on the enemy. This effect is enhanced when the target is in a <color=#FF8741>[Break]</color> state, making them especially effective against enemies with a <color=#FF8741>[Break Gauge]</color>. When their MP is depleted, switch them out with another <color=#AF64AF>Dark</color> ally to allow them to recover their MP while sidelined, then put them back into battle once they're recharged.

Draw Support
- An SSR is guaranteed to appear within 80 draws, and the count will reset upon obtaining the hunter.
- Starting with the 64th draw of the Draw Support, the draw rate of the SSR increases by 5.8% each time.
- When acquiring an SSR from the Draw Support, the selected SSR hunter has a 2/3 chance of being acquired, while the other unselected SSR hunter has a 1/3 chance of being acquired.
- If you obtain an SSR hunter that wasn't selected from the Draw Support, your next attempt on the Draw Support will guarantee the selected SSR hunter.

It.StringStory.302030041_FRR:
As a child, Fern lost everything to war. She was on the brink of ending her own life when Heiter the Priest rescued her and raised her as his own.

While Hieter was alive, Fern had one goal: to become someone worthwhile. "Learning to live on my own is my way of repaying his kindness. I want him to be glad that he saved my life."

After succeeding in piercing a massive stone with magic, a goal set by Heiter, Fern parted ways with him and joined Frieren on her journey as an apprentice.

Along the journey, Fern's abilities grew stronger. Her skills in magic control and observation reached heights that impress even the talented Frieren.

During the second part of her First-Class Mage Exam, her staff was broken beyond repair, and she argued with Frieren when Frieren told her to discard her old staff and buy a new one. Fern could not imagine throwing away her staff, as it had been a gift from Hieter and with her since childhood.

Frieren's lack of emotional sensitivity caused a misunderstanding and, troubled, Frieren visited Richter, the owner of a magic shop, to have the staff repaired. Seeing the state of the staff, Richter initially balked, but Frieren persuaded him to give the repair a try.

"It's a fine staff, meticulously crafted. It must've been deeply cherished."

It.StringStory.302020028:
"I will protect my country."

Her raw passion and natural competitiveness were her driving forces. Those virtues helped her grow as a hunter faster than anyone else. She was proud of every one of her numerous battle scars and wore them like medals. They were, after all, proof of her efforts to stand side by side with her role model.

"The path he takes is for his country."

Even as he began to stray from that path, she continued to follow in his footsteps, willing to overlook the obvious.

"A hero never walks on the wrong path." She assured herself.

But when all the facts were laid bare, she had to make a choice. Was she going to ignore who he had become and keep walking his path of lies? Or was she going to chase her original beliefs?

"There are no heroes whose footsteps are worthy of following anymore. So I'll have to forge my own path."

It.StringStory.302020030:
He once had conviction in his beliefs.

He was stronger than any other hunter in his nation, and he felt he represented Japan. He thought that he didn't need to play political games: he could protect his country with his own power rather than ascending to a throne built on sacrifices.

But nothing in this world remains the same, and his steadfast perspective eventually became distorted by his pride.

The weak are always taken advantage of.

"I won't let the world write me off so easily. The only things that matter are what I have to protect... and what I need to maintain."

"I will get what I deserve."

Not even other S-Ranks dare to look down on the very strongest: a National Level hunter's power is equivalent to the power of a nation.

So when a stained hand was extended to him, he shook it. Though the things that needed to be protected were the reason he started down the path, and his desire for respect became his immoral compass.

"The National Level title is the position that befits my powers."

It.StringStory.302020023:
People have always been quick to comment on how she looks or what she's wearing.

But Gina lives by her own standards, not theirs.

"Don't let narrow-minded people get to you. People who only look skin-deep aren't looking at the real you."

Over time, she built up standards about who would earn her trust.

They can't judge people by appearance alone.

They have to really value other people.

They have to stand up for what's right.

And if she ever met someone who would would check all those boxes, she was sure they would be able to overcome anything together.

"I can get through anything as long as I have someone I can trust watching my back."

It.StringStory.302020022:
Their peaceful, everyday lives were like a dream. And just like a dream, they ended too soon.

When the gates started appearing around the orphanage...

When no one came to take care of them...

When Sister Millie left the church alone...

And finally, when she saw Sister Millie's gruesome wounds as she stumbled back to them.

It was then that Charlotte realized.

It was time to wake up.

She didn't know what nightmares were yet to come.

"Guard the children of the church. It's your duty as protectors."

Sister Millie had given her that job. She had to fulfill it.

"I could really use two little helpers like you..."

"...Okay."

It.StringStory.302020021:
BANG!

Harper had been split seconds from pulling the trigger. Now, she looked back in surprise.

Sister Millie's trembling arms had pointed the gun at X.

"Now skipping a turn... that's against the rules!"

A hail of bullets riddled Sister Millie's body.

The corners of her mouth twitched helplessly as she fell, staining the ground of the dungeon with a blanket of red.

A giant doll grabbed the howling Harper as she tried to lunge at the killer.

She struggled with all her might, but Harper couldn't get away.

She shrieked, tears streaming down her face.

Finally, as they fled, Sister Millie's last words seemed to reach her ears.

"Run... live your lives..."

It.StringStory.302020027:
Every day was the same. Nothing moved and nothing changed. She minded her manners and followed the orders echoing in her mind. Everything in her life was stagnant until it was acted upon by an outside force.

"Can I trust you?"
"I'd like to borrow her for a bit."

She didn't know why, but the moment she saw him, she felt relief. When she reached the end of her journey, unable to sort out the conflicting emotions and the commands in her head, Esil's arm moved without her realizing it.

"Jinwoo, sir! I...!"

Esil watched the spear fly toward the demon king as she finally found her answer. This single emotion was worth protecting... even if she had to betray everything else.

And that was...

It.StringStory.302020026:
Whether she was at school or at home, Shimizu's younger sister always looked lonely. For all the things that changed when magic beasts started appearing, that wasn't one of them.

"Himari, are you sure you're okay?"
"Of course. You can tell me about all the things I'm missing out on, right? Then it's like I'm not missing out on anything at all."

Noise and chaos engulfed the festival that day as the monsters swarmed the streets. As Himari stood between them and her sister, Shimizu made up her mind:

"I'll make you happy no matter what."

Do gods exist? Shimizu still wasn't sure, but she knew then that it didn't matter to her. Gods or no, she would do whatever it took to make her younger sister happy, even if it meant risking her life at every moment.

It.StringStory.302020024:
Her best intentions always led to the worst outcomes.

When she tried to give an old lady directions, kick a soccer ball back to some players, bring drinks to her classmates, and even when she tried to warn a friend that they might get hurt, everything ended badly.

"Why is it always me...?"

"Everyone ends up unhappy because of me."

The pattern of misfortunes dragged her down even further.

Finally she decided to just do as the cards told her. The cards would show her the way forward.

For a long time, Isla stopped making decisions on her own. Then, she was met with some unexpected luck.

"With my friends... a bright future is sure to come!"

<color=#FAC800>[Light]</color> Striker

When their <color=#FAC800>Ultimate Skill</color> is active, the effects of all their skills are enhanced and the <color=#64FAC8>[Shield]</color> effect, which was previously only granted during skill animations, is kept even after the animations are done.

When the user uses their <color=#FAC800>Ultimate Skill</color> again while the state is already active, they can deal incredible amount of damage. This ability synergizes well with team members who can grant <color=#64FAC8>[Shields]</color>.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc030:
She hadn't seen her young cousin in any of his usual spots. Joohee remembered her cousin mentioning that he was going fishing with the neighborhood children. He'd left early in the morning, without even eating breakfast. She began searching the streams and the ridges of the rice fields, but she couldn't find her cousin anywhere.

Where else could they have gone fishing? Joohee thought hard, and recalled that she often heard the sounds of flowing water while on the trail leading to the forest- near the location where she found the gate.

If a Dungeon Break had occurred, and monsters were wandering the forest, then her cousin and the children...

She began to imagine the worst. She tried to calm her mind as she returned to the gate.

She was right to worry.

Just outside the gate, she saw a meandering Werewolf.

Lee Joohee quickly turned behind a tree and covered her mouth to prevent her breath from escaping.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc031:
She needed a plan. Could she move to the stream without making a sound? The Hunters Association needed to be notified immediately, but how soon could the hunters possibly arrive? Her mind went as blank as a sheet of paper. Time passed as Joohee stood still, paralyzed by indecision, hand lingering over the Hunters Association's number in her phone.

Then she heard a scream. She snapped back to reality. She looked back at where the Werewolf had been to find a trail of footprints headed towards the stream.

Swallowing her fear, she crept toward the stream as carefully as possible. Scattered around the stream were what was left of the other children... the back of her cousin's head trembling as he hid between the rocks.

The Werewolf had left, having lost interest in the now-still children.

Joohee ran to her cousin. He was sprawled out on the ground, gasping for air.

Unsure of what to do, Joohee extended a hand to stop the bleeding... and the wound began to heal all on its own.

However, the injuries were deep, and they had been left to bleed out into the stream. Her cousin's breathing was getting weaker.

Lee Joohee threw him onto her shoulders and started running down the mountain.

She couldn't think until she arrived back at the village. There, she saw the armed hunters and well-dressed Hunters Association employees. The Werewolf lay dead in front of them, its head severed.

The hunters who spotted Joohee began to take her and her cousin's vitals. As their faces grew solemn, Lee Joohee knew she had arrived too late.

"Giving up is not an option. There's only relentless perseverance."

Hunters who wield swords are a dime a dozen, but Sugimoto Reiji's swordsmanship follows a different path. Striking like lightning and raging like a storm, his swordsmanship is truly unmatched.

Three splinters of emotions bind him to this sword: pride that will not bend before authority, bitterness born of loss, and the soul-piercing emptiness he felt as he watched his predecessor fail.

"From this moment on, I'll be in charge of the Blade Guild."

These three emotions fused together and forged Reiji into who he is today. Even in moments when the crushing weight of responsibility threatens to break him, it's those very merciless emotions that force him back to his feet and drive his hand to the hilt of his sword.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc033:
Maybe she had already known. Maybe she had felt his breath stop, and tried to ignore it.

She blamed herself for not going to help her cousin sooner.

A Hunters Association employee tried to comfort her, telling her that they were able to arrive early: the town could have been destroyed if they hadn't happened to have been dispatched for a mission nearby. The hunter reminded her that it wasn't her fault, and that she had saved the town, but she wasn't comforted.

After the incident had been resolved, she was questioned about the gate, the children, and the Werewolf. It was then that she was told that she, too, could be a hunter. But she couldn't bring herself to use that power.

Joohee buried her memories of that day when she buried her cousin. At least, that is, until Woo Jinchul visited her three years later.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc023:
No amount of talent can beat hard work, but no amount of hard work can beat someone who enjoys doing it for a living.

This was Lim Tae-Gyu's mantra.

He wasn't the most talented player, but he enjoyed tennis more than anyone else.

His passion bolstered his talent and inspired him to excel: regardless of who his opponent was, in order to fully enjoy the match, he had to possess skills to compete with them.

Every time he stepped out on to the court, he was calm and composed. He was happy to just to play. What did he have to worry about?

Some mistook his demeanor for arrogance, but Tae-Gyu never really thought much of it. He wasn't really interested in clearing up those misunderstandings.

He was only interested in playing, and he would be satisfied with the result, no matter what it was. As an athlete, these were the only two things that really mattered to him.

To keep his family alive, he had to survive at all costs. He couldn't die and leave his wife and child behind.

Why did he forget his rules? Even though he regretted his choices, he had no choice but to face the fact he had entrusted his life to an uncertain plan, thought up by The Weakest Hunter of All Mankind.

1. During certain attack phases, Kamish will <color=#BF9DFF>attempt to enhance</color> either its wings or tail. These body parts become <color=#FEBD21>vulnerable</color>, allowing them to be attacked for a limited time.

2. The vulnerable body parts can only be attacked with <color=#FF8741>Break</color> and <color=#FF8741>Elemental Accumulation</color>. Failure to reduce those body parts' HP within a certain time will cause the <color=#BF9DFF>parts to be enhanced</color>.

3. When all of Kamish's <color=#BF9DFF>parts are enhanced</color> during battle, Kamish will use Annihilation Descent.

4. Use <color=#FF8741>Breaks</color> and <color=#FF8741>Elemental Accumulation</color> during its <color=#FEBD21>vulnerable phase</color> to stop its enhancement quickly. Destroy its parts to prevent it from using Annihilation Descent.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc034:
Low-ranking gates appear more frequently than their high-ranking counterparts. As a result, simply by a matter of numbers, low-ranking gates are the source of most Dungeon Breaks.

In one particular neighborhood, a D-Rank gate was not dealt with for a full week, despite the residents' numerous protests.

Hunters only arrived at the scene after the fact, and their teamwork was awkward at best and disastrous at worst.

Certainly, they were able to cull the monsters, but the hunters were pulled together at the last minute, and they had made several noticeable mistakes.

After the boss was killed, the gate closed, and the hunters' crew moved off to the next location. The residents were finally able to breathe a sigh of relief and return to their homes.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc022:
However, Yoonho disagreed with Lim Tae-Gyu over how the guild should grow and the distribution of profits. Lim Tae-Gyu wanted to expand the guild, and Yoonho wanted the guild members to receive a bigger profit share.

In the end, when they couldn't come to an agreement, Baek Yoonho took the members that sided with him and established a new guild: the White Tiger Guild.

Things went smoothly after that.

The guild grew well - after all, people no longer called his ability "a magic beast trick" or thought of him as "a magic beast spy."

But Yoonho tried not to use his Beast Transformation very often, now that he was a leader- he knew how people viewed both his natural appearance and his ability.

In response, an urban legend began surrounding Baek Yoonho and magical threats in Korea.

They say, if Baek Yoonho ever appears fully transformed, that can only mean a tremendously powerful magic beast is nearby, so it's time to run!

After that, Han Song-Yi desperately searched for a party that would take her, but no one in their right mind would bring an E-Rank high schooler into a dungeon.

Dejected, she turned to the Hunters Association for help, but they also rejected her. They said they would consider her application once she'd graduated.

But she wouldn't give up. Eventually, she found someone willing to take her on raids...

but there was a strange condition: She didn't actually need to go inside the gates. They were paying her to just show up and stand outside to fill the headcount requirement. She didn't care, though.

Having nineteen C-Rank Gate clears under her belt would surely help her progress in her hunter career.

Her confidence surged as she watched Sung Jinwoo, a fellow E-Rank Hunter, complete the raids by himself.

However, after surviving the Red Gate incident, she realized that her confidence was entirely unfounded. Sung Jinwoo didn't clear those gates because he was an E-Rank hunter; he cleared them because he was Sung Jinwoo.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc035:
Song Chiyul and his family were among those residents. He had asked the Hunters Association staff if they had done a sweep to make sure the area was completely safe and didn't receive a straight answer, but with the gate closed, he thought nothing of it.

He was assured that D-Rank dungeons had only weaker monsters, and the hunters on the scene were very experienced.

But something was still bothering him. To put his mind to rest, he did his own sweep of his house, checking every room... a decision he regrets to this day.

While he was inside, he heard screams coming from his front yard. He quickly grabbed his wooden sword and ran outside. His children lay still in the grass while a group of goblins targeted his wife.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc021:
This is the perfect place for me.

As his bewildered target started to question him, Taeshik drove a dagger into his target's body and watched them crumple.

He methodically twisted the knife in his fallen target.

When he left the Gate, he blended into the crowd, hiding the possessions he'd swiped, including a shiny rock inscribed with a strange pattern.

Four years later, Taeshik's skills got him hired at the Hunters Association.

He gained respect for his eagerness to go out into the field, and no one questioned why the survival rate of his raids was so low.

Thus, he was able to continue his "hunter-hunting" habit...

At least, until he ran into Sung Jinwoo.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc051:
It was all very ironic.

The flames which had set him back at key moments in his life had now unlocked the door to being the strongest hunter in Korea.

He now had a suspicion that a hunter's abilities were determined by their most traumatic memories or their greatest regrets.

If true, it meant that every time a hunter faced off against a monster, they would fight out of desperation, not duty- their abilities would remind them that they were fighting to ensure their greatest mistakes weren't repeated. As smart and perceptive as Choi Jong-In was, he was also excellent at compartmentalizing.

This was no time to be sentimental. He set the thought aside.

Regardless of how he obtained his power, this was the opportunity he'd been waiting for. In fact, it was the mother of all opportunities. Even if his awakening was caused by past misfortunes, he was determined to not make them the defining feature of his future.

Awakening or not, that side of him hadn't changed: there was no reason to examine the past instead of thinking of a way forward.

He leveraged his fame and power as an 'S-Rank hunter' until he was staring at the guild master certification and the veritable mountain of business cards on his desk. It was time to get to work.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc045:
After that, Han Song-Yi desperately searched for a party that would take her, but no one in their right mind would bring an E-Rank high schooler into a dungeon. Dejected, she turned to the Hunters Association for help, but they also rejected her. They said they would consider her application once she'd graduated.

But she wouldn't give up. Eventually, she found someone willing to take her on raids... but there was a strange condition: She didn't actually need to go inside the gates. They were paying her to just show up and stand outside to fill the headcount requirement. She didn't care, though. Having nineteen C-Rank gate clears under her belt would surely help her progress in her hunter career.

Her confidence surged as she watched Sung Jinwoo, a fellow E-Rank Hunter, complete the raids by himself.

However, after surviving the Red Gate incident, she realized that her confidence was entirely unfounded. Sung Jinwoo didn't clear those gates because he was an E-Rank hunter; he cleared them because he was Sung Jinwoo.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc036:
He knew in his head that ordinary people weren't a match for even the weakest of monsters, but he had no time to consider other options.

Wooden sword in hand, he rushed the goblins.

He was confident in his swordsmanship.
He had competed in international kendo tournaments. He had won medals and trophies. He thought he could take down a couple of small goblins.

He was wrong.

No matter how many hits he landed against the goblins, they shrugged them all off. They slowly but surely landed blow after blow against him, until one of them finally brought him down to his knees.

By this point, his wife had fallen silent. He instinctively knew that it was the end of the road for him as well.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc020:
He set out in search of a victim. But when he finally closed in on his selected target, they were whisked away into a cerulean vortex right before his eyes.

He immediately thought of the "blue portals" he had heard about on the news.

Only the chosen could enter, and those who did not return swiftly were lost forever.

Curious, he took a tentative step forward.

Their exclusivity had been greatly exaggerated, and he easily slipped into the gate.

There, he saw his target fighting off a horde of magic beasts.

Though his frightened target's movements were clumsy, the magic beasts were steadily decreasing in number.

It was only after the fight had ended that his target noticed he had arrived.

Kang Taeshik put on his best "helpless civilian" act and approached.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc044:
Ever since gates, dungeons, and monsters became the new normal, schoolchildren began to dream of being heroes like the hunters they saw in the media. If you asked a random student on the street what their dream job is, most of them would reply "Hunter."

In that regard, Han Song-Yi wasn't all that different from other kids her age. She dreamed of having a spectacular life like the high-ranking hunters she saw on TV.

Fortunately for her, she was able to take one step closer to becoming a hunter when she turned nineteen.

Han Song-Yi suddenly felt a faint power inside her, just like she'd heard about on the internet. She immediately went to get evaluated. Even though she received E-Rank, the lowest rank possible, she was still qualified to join raids.

It.StringStory.302030032:
It's easy to abandon responsibility. You simply look away and go back to your life.

But the cost of ignoring it is great.

Lennart Niermann still remembers that night. He witnessed a thirteen-year-old child forced to fight a magic beast alone. As he descended the mountain, carrying his younger brother on his back, he made a resolute promise.

He promised to never to turn a blind eye again.

The strong must protect the weak.

Even if he could one day be overwhelmed and his resistance became nothing more than a meaningless sacrifice...

"An honorable death is better than a shameful life!"

He chose to carry the weight of responsibility as long as he lived.

It.StringStory.302030044:
He always stood in the center of the victor's spotlight. He led everyone, proved his strategy, and was celebrated for their victory.

"Follow my lead. A perfect victory is our only goal."

All followed him to victory. His path was illuminated only by dazzling glory. But ahead was the first defeat he would ever face.

"Why won't you listen to me?"

To them, his strategy was a delusion. After the battle, when only ashes remained, he was completely excluded.

"What I needed was a team that listened."

If he were given another chance along with a perfect team.

"My strategy never fails."

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc037:
He tried to force his body to move, to lead them inside and burn down the house, just so that the goblins would not escape to attack another family.

Then, just as their teeth were about to close in on his neck, an arrow pierced one of the goblin's skulls.

Through hazy vision, he looked up to see a woman running to his aid, striking down the goblins one by one.

This was the last thing he saw before he woke up at the hospital. He was immediately bombarded with questions from all sorts of media outlets wanting to run his story, with or without his input.

Soon after, the hunters and Hunters Association staff involved with the raid came to him with their heads bowed. Some of them even came back and visited him every day. At first, he could not bring himself to forgive them. He threw whatever he could get his hands on at them in fits of rage, but eventually, his anger ebbed and he began to focus his energies on the more fundamental issues.
Story.CharacterInfo_Desc027:
Even as he founded and led a monolithic guild with his comrades-in-arms, and even as he was called to Jeju Island to deal with the first S-Rank gate, he never forgot to have fun.

But the Jeju Island raid killed many of his dear teammates. Suddenly, he was forced to confront the sobering truth.

Fighting results in death. And death isn't fun.

The monsters they faced weren't playing a game. They were intelligent, brutal beings that cared about nothing outside of killing hunters. No amount of preparation or training could truly protect you against them; because they didn't care about playing fair.

One moment of hesitation or the slightest mistake was all it took. And when you lose to monsters, there are no rematches. You never get to play again.

The fact that his failure to grasp such a simple concept cost him the lives of his closest comrades tormented him. But regrets do not bring back the dead. These days, Tae-Gyu steps onto the battlefield with a new resolve.

Fighting is no longer a game to him. There is no more fun. And if he forgets, it is the voices of his dead friends that he hears reminding him: It matters if you win or lose.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc057:
There was a live broadcast of a horrific scene inside an amusement park. Wounded hunters lay agonized on the ground, and citizens ran around aimlessly, screaming for help.

The last shot of the broadcast was oddly calm... it showed a boy, staring glassy-eyed at the empty space where the gate had been.

Woo Jinchul later learned that the boy's father was a hunter who had gone in to rescue the others. Thanks to his efforts, all of his comrades were accounted for: he was the only one who didn't make it back.

The lost hunter was quite famous. Even someone as unplugged as Jinchul knew his name.

It was meant to be an uplifting story: The hunters saved the day yet again, suffering casualties, but ultimately driving back the monsters that poured from the gate. But all Woo Jinchul saw was the sacrifices made that day and a boy who'd lost his father.

Just as Choi Jong-In had predicted, the dramatic changes to the world did bring about new business opportunities.

Raw Mana Crystals and Essence Stones could be turned into building materials and brought in unbelievable profits. Through the connections he had made, people had come to trust him as someone who could keep a secret.

He knew very well that networking was the key to success. Networking brought him information, and information is power... and money.

The career he'd been kindling before couldn't hold a candle to this new lucrative one. Distracted, Jong-In didn't notice that something was changing in him.

It took a life-or-death experience to bring his powers to light.

Fieldwork was always dangerous. In order to protect civilians, there were strict rules that governed who could enter a gate.

But six years is a long time- long enough for even the greatest of dangers to become commonplace.

It's an unfortunate side-effect of humanity's incredible adaptability: though the dungeons never got less dangerous, the longer they were around, the better people got at ignoring the risks. Especially when recklessness could make you a pretty penny.

It.StringStory.302030035:
Her beloved friends fell right before her eyes. She had failed to protect them.

The memory of her inadequacy resurfaced each night, drenching her life in regret. Even when it didn't rain, endless streams of pain flowed in Jinah's muddied heart.

"I want to be someone who can face monsters and fight back without fear. Like Dad and this hunter."

Finally, Jinah took up her weapon. Her attacks were a dance, and the steps were choreographed by her past shame and future promises.

Jinah changed. Though burdened with grief, her resolve now remained unshaken. She battled faster than the wind and more violently than a storm.

It.StringStory.302030045:
A knight born of common blood. Behind his back lurked the judgement and contempt of the noble class.

The wealthy believed that Knighthood was meant for the aristocrats alone and a common-born knight was a thorn in their side.

Never gaining his peers' respect, the man was always sent to the front lines. He was sent to die, but instead humbly swung his sword with pure conviction.

Before the swiftly flying blades, he never retreated. Before the rain of arrows, he never faltered.

He swung hundreds of times and cut through thousands. The massive sword in the man's hands drew a crimson trail.

The battlefield was dyed crimson, as if swallowed by a scarlet sunset. The blood-soaked greatsword gleamed in the calloused hands of the exhausted man.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc038:
The major guilds only wanted to use their manpower and resources to clear the high-ranking dungeons for profit. And the Hunters Association who handled most of the low-ranked dungeons were bleeding members.

After all, who would want to do more dangerous work for lower pay? The problem was the lack of resources and manpower to ensure that tragedies like this wouldn't happen over and over again.

How could one man be able to stop it? What could he possibly do?

He had his answer before long.

Song Chiyul's powers awoke. Oddly enough, though he had spent his entire life devoted to the sword, he developed a gift for spellcasting. Regardless, he welcomed any power that would help him achieve his goals.

As a mage, he was sought out by many decently-sized guilds, but he turned down every one and instead elected to form a neighborhood watch, with hunters who had survived similar experiences and had refused to join the guilds.

They would be the ones to work with the Hunters Association to close the lower-rank gates. And they would be sure not to make any mistakes.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc026:
In the days before the hunter scene had any structure, any particularly strong hunter could garner media attention and become an overnight celebrity.

Lim Tae-Gyu was one such hunter.

His arrows always landed between the eyes of his enemies, and no Magic Beast would survive venturing within the range of his bow.

The rumors grew out of control: it was said that a single one of his arrows could kill ten monsters. He did his best to live up to the public's expectations.

Of course, he never abandoned his theory that talent and hard work could never beat enjoyment.

Repeatedly facing the unpredictable trajectory of a tennis ball had been the perfect training tool for the ever-changing, chaotic nature of the battlefield.

He even felt that the more chaotic the situation was, the more fun it would be.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc054:
Four years ago, he had used another hunter as a shield in order to survive a dungeon. He had survived, but never forgave himself.

Still... Doing the wrong thing is hard the first time, but easy the second.

So when fate brought them together again- he and the people he abandoned- he felt that the time had come to pay for his choices.

He had committed unforgivable sins. He would have to pay the price.

He thought the first step might be a proper apology to Sung Jinwoo. Maybe then he could become the honest hunter he longed to be.

But he never got the chance.
Story.CharacterInfo_Desc046:
Despite wielding fire magic on a daily basis, Choi Jong-In is uncomfortable around fire. Over the course of his life, many of his greatest misfortunes involved fire.

For example, his house once caught on fire due to a minor mistake in the electrical wiring, his office was nearly destroyed by a fire that had spread from the neighboring store, and he almost lost an eye when a firecracker misfired directly into his face.

Although fire had caused him to suffer time and time again, he'd thought nothing of it and believed that his incendiary misfortunes were just part of the average trials and tribulations of life.

Incomprehensible things happened every day, after all. He had his hands so full trying to keep up with these constant dramatic changes, that he was never able to spend much time dwelling on his past troubles.

He'd rather use his time to do something productive. Change leads to opportunity, and monumental changes were happening all the time. To him, there was no reason to examine the past instead of thinking of a way forward.

Choi Jong-In works tirelessly to improve his life and the lives of those around him, blissfully unaware that he is actually playing with fire.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc039:
Everyone has dreamed of turning their life around at least once. Jo Kyuhwan watched the S-Rank hunters on TV and dreamed of what his life could be like if he could be like them.

Sure, awakening wasn't something he could just do. He also knew that even if he beat the odds, he probably wouldn't be a high-ranking hunter unless he was chosen by the heavens.

That's why, instead of aiming for the moon, he aimed for goals he felt he could reach.

"If I could just be a B-Rank hunter, no more, no less than that, wouldn't that be enough?" He mused. A-Rank and S-Rank were beyond what he dared to dream about...

It was a small dream, so he thought it wouldn't be so strange if it actually came true. Unfortunately, even that dream was more than he got.

He learned that others like him were using their awakened powers to fight the mysterious monsters that had been emerging from the gates.

The media called them heroes. Despite the ever-increasing number of casualties, the praise for the "hunters" never faltered.

Tae-Gyu had found his new calling. If he was forced off the path of sports by his power, then he just needed to wield his newfound power to forge a new path for himself.

Filled with determination, he stepped on to his first battlefield and immediately felt that he had been right.

Fighting monsters was just as enjoyable as hitting a striped yellow ball over past the other player. He could do this all day.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc055:
In the bygone era of nine years ago, when the contents of the gates were still unknown...

Hunters fought the monsters not for profit, but simply to protect others.

However, as a college student, Woo Jinchul did not care much about the much-romanticized dungeons and hunters, no matter how frequently they were on the news.
Story.CharacterInfo_Desc041:
Misery was Hwang Dongsuk's childhood companion.

When he was fifteen, his parents died in a car accident, and he and his brother were left in the care of their grandmother. She suffered from a chronic illness and died soon thereafter.

He saw the negligent driver that killed his parents get off with a warning. The driver never even apologized to the two young boys of the family they destroyed.

Caring for Dongsuk and Dongsoo caused their grandmother to neglect her own illness, expediting her death.

By this point, Dongsuk knew that his family's poverty was at the root of it all.

As he once again put on a black tie to stand alone at an empty funeral, he asked himself why the whole sorry chain of events had been set into motion. He knew who was to blame: his family's poverty. The world itself.

So he went after revenge. His brother Dongsoo readily followed his lead as they dove into a life of crime.

Dongsuk had a never-ending list of ideas for ways to make a killing, and Dongsoo would always faithfully carry them out.

It.StringStory.302030047:
The girl always believed the world was cold. She spent the winter in a chilly room in the orphanage, huddled together with the other children.

"We're like penguins."

They stayed huddled together until Meri found her true family. On the day of the reunion, standing in the heart of their misfortune, Meri came to understand.

You can't protect anyone by simply holding back.

"Being a monster doesn't give me the right to make my friends suffer."

White snow swirled behind her. On a night pierced by a biting wind, the girl raised the heavy saw blade.

"I lived through the harsh winters."
"It's thanks to my friends, who gave me the same warmth as a real family."
"So... leave them alone."
"And... it's best not to look down on me."

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc024:
His outlook on life only started to change when the gates appeared.

Even though he couldn't explain why or how, he was able to sense and harness the "mana" flowing around him.

At first, he thought that anyone could learn to use it, but he soon realized just how special his power was.

He saw his newfound abilities as a curse. Now that he was capable of things beyond the power of an ordinary human, he could no longer enjoy his tennis matches.

What fun is there in playing a game where the victor is always decided? His powers made it impossible for him to follow the core tenant of sportsmanship: fair play.

Robbed of his sole source of enjoyment in life, he looked elsewhere for meaning.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc040:
He was a C-Rank Mage-type awakened being.

Compared to the number of Physical-types out there, Mage-type and Support-type hunters were rare. If he honed his skills, he might have a chance at joining a major guild.

But the ranks are absolute. Even if he could join a major guild, there's no way to get any stronger.

High-ranking awakened beings would always outclass him.

He was beyond disappointed. Kyuhwan started feeling that this was unfair. He'd awoken, but he would never have the chance to make more money or get better benefits.

If he was going to risk his life every day for what little he could get as a C-Rank, why wouldn't he just do something else?

So he gave up on joining a guild.

But when he met Hwang Dongsuk, his perspective changed. He could make a lot more if he became Hwang Dongsuk's right-hand man. And thus, he happily took charge of handling the "bait."

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc043:
Hwang Dongsuk knew an opportunity when he saw one.

Even before becoming an awakened being, he'd been convicted of fraud several times for claiming insurance money for fake magic beast run-ins, holding "awakening classes" for children while masquerading as the Hunters Association, and many more gate-related schemes.

After becoming an awakened being, he would regularly bring "bait" onto a raid and treat the hired hunters like disposable tools.

But crime never pays. When you live your life by the principle of "survival of the fittest," you have to be ready for the day that you're no longer the biggest fish. Eventually, a would-be victim finally took him down.

Maybe justice has a sense of humor.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc058:
He thought long and hard about it. The reason why he had wanted to become an officer of the law was not because of petty fascination or admiration. More than anything, he wanted to save people from the evils of others.

But while he watched and rewatched the scenes from the amusement park, only one question was going through his head: hunters put their lives on the line to protect the people, but who protects the hunters?

At the time, hunters had just begun to form guilds to better handle the dungeons, but there was never any news about protections or services offered to hunters.

As he learned more and more about the subject, he was filled with a strong desire to right this wrong. Society expected so much from hunters, yet provided them with so little. When he heard the news that Go Gunhee, a business owner-turned-hunter, was forming a Hunters Association modeled after the USA's Federal Bureau of Hunters, he knew what he had to do.
Story.CharacterInfo_Desc042:
Each time things went as planned, they would try to make the next job even bigger. They swindled countless people out of their money and left them saddled with debt.

A life of crime comes with its consequences. Dongsuk spent a lot of time going in and out of jail. But he never repented- or even questioned himself. Not even when his victims cried or screamed about how deeply he had hurt them.

They suffered because they were weak. They were stupid, poor, and powerless to stop him.

That's how the world was meant to be. He had no intention of obeying the rules of a society that so thoroughly abandoned him and his brother. Society never rewards the good; only those who can get away with more than their fair share.

It was a twisted philosophy, but with no one there to correct him, Hwang Dongsuk couldn't step off the path he had forged for himself.

Not long after, the "gates" began to appear.

There was no better setting for their work than places that would vanish forever, taking all evidence of what had transpired inside with them.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc029:
She'd heard about these so-called "gates" on the evening news. This one was no bigger than the ones she'd seen in pictures, but she instinctively knew that it was trouble.

With shaking hands, Lee Joohee dialed the Hunters Association's number and reported the gate, snapping a picture as proof. But the words of an article that she'd read a couple of days before entered her mind.

It had said that gates found in the less-populous countryside were often pushed down on the priority list and tended to not be closed fast enough, causing "Dungeon Breaks" that could devastate rural communities.

Until the hunters arrived to close the gate, she needed to warn the townsfolk and get them to evacuate.

Lee Joohee didn't know much about them, but she knew that the magic beasts that came out of the gates could not be defeated by ordinary humans. She hurried to tell the townsfolk.

Only after everyone had gotten ready to leave was she finally able to return to her grandmother's house. Her grandmother was away, so she hurriedly packed all of their things... and was hit with a sinking feeling.

It.StringStory.302030043:
Standing a step behind the rest, veiled in shadow, she waits. Within the quiet depths of darkness, she answers someone's question.

"As a child, I thought my life was the darkest and loneliest of all."

An empty home, endless waiting, and countless lonely dinners. Still, she knew that those she loved would step back through the doorway some day.

"And then I realized something. You know, every light casts a shadow."

For their sake, she accepted the darkness, always standing behind, ready to help, and even when they drifted away, she would wait.

"In the end, your glory is my joy."

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc028:
Lee Joohee was still in high school when she was evaluated as an "awakened being."

Four years ago, the July heat hit record-breaking highs. Joohee was out for a light walk in the countryside, as always did while on vacation.

She stayed in the area for about a week around the same time every year, and had a favorite set of walking trails.

She went slowly and leisurely, appreciating the familiar scenery. Finding the smallest changes in the seemingly unchanging landscape somehow gave her hope that everything can grow, with time.

That's why she loved taking walks in the countryside.

But for some reason, on that particular day, she felt compelled to leave the path. As if she were being guided by an invisible hand, Joohee entered the depths of the forest.

The "change" that she discovered was anything but small. It was a whirlpool of blue light, hidden in the bushes.

I would allow my family to become hunters if they're determined to be Awakened Beings.

It was one of the questions in the hunter survey that was conducted sometime ago.

The result was very interesting, as more than 80 percent of hunters said they would be against their family members working as hunters.

Considering that most students' dream was to be one, the result was a bit ironic.

Han Song-Yi was no different from other students her age.

The glamorous lives of high-ranking hunters shown on TV were just objects of admiration for the young girl.

Unfortunately, Han Song-Yi didn't have a "hunter family" to oppose her becoming a hunter.

On the day she turned 19, Han Song-Yi felt a faint surge of power, like the stories posted online.

She got evaluated immediately. Even though she received the lowest rank of E, she was happy: she had become a hunter.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc048:
People started making secret deals. Reporters would often slip site supervisors a "cover charge" to get a closer look at a gate.

People who wanted to trade with Choi Jong-In would also come to these sites with cash in unmarked envelopes. Smaller guilds often couldn't finish hauling goods out of the dungeon before they needed to defeat the boss, only bringing out a small portion of the Mana Crystals or Essence Stones due to the lack of manpower. The operation he supervised was routine: grab the Magic Beast corpses left behind by a smaller guild, and get out.

But a bit of negligence and a lack of hunters turned what would have been a small incident into a full-blown disaster. The gate should have been dormant for a couple more days, but monsters started pouring out one after another, and the situation outside devolved into chaos.

It was a C-Rank gate.

It shouldn't have been a difficult dungeon for them, but even as a swarm of large cobalt golems came charging through the gate, no hunters followed.

At this point, it was clear that the raid team had either missed an entire area, or everyone was dead.

Choi Jong-In had the presence of mind to immediately find a hiding place, racking his brain for a way out while also trying his hardest to ignore the harrowing screams all around him.

The gate had spawned inside a shallow cave, so there was only one exit.

It.StringStory.302030042_FRR:
Orphaned by war at a young age, Stark was taken in by the Warrior Eisen and raised as his first apprentice. Under his tutelage, Stark learned everything about being a warrior. However, one day during training, Eisen beat Stark out of fear of his exceptional talent. This led to a fight between them, and afterwards, Stark left Eisen without a word.

Stark is a coward who faints or freezes in the face of strong foes and threatening situations, but his pure heart can never ignore those in need. Before fighting the Solar Dragon, he was paralyzed by fear in the face of danger, but continued training regardless, determined to protect the village.

"I'm Stark, this village's hero."
"I must protect the village."

Fern once told a cowardly Stark,
"All you need is resolve. What you've put work into building won't leave you so easily."

Determined to protect the village, Stark faced the dragon with trembling hands.
"All I need... is resolve."

At last, Stark defeated the dragon, all by himself. The great warrior, now capable of fighting for others, continued his journey with Frieren so that he could one day return to his mentor, bringing with him tales of his countless journeys.

SysConstStr.SelectPickUp_SelectGuide_Pol:
This is a function that increases your chance of drawing SSRs on your Selection List.
The Selection List can be changed at any time.

Draw Support
- An SSR is guaranteed to appear within 70 draws, and the count will reset upon acquisition.
- Starting with the 60th draw of the Draw Support, the draw rate of the SSR increases by 5.8% each time.
- When acquiring an SSR from the Draw Support, there is a 50% chance of acquiring one of the 2 SSRs on your Selection List, with equal odds of acquiring any particular one on the list, and a 50% chance of acquiring an SSR not on the list, divided equally among the other available items.
- If the SSR you obtain through Draw Support is not on your Selection List, there's a 50% chance to obtain 1 of the 2 SSRs on the Selection List on your next Draw Support attempt.
