It.StringStory.302030037_IDLE2:
She used to be fascinated by robots, superheroes, and magical creatures. At least before the supernatural turned out to be real. Back then, she was studying at a prestigious school. She excelled in academics. She later received a fairly high hunter rank, too. But through these systems, no one heard what she really dreamed of.

"What I really want to do... is something else."

As time passed, the long-awaited news finally arrived. She accepted the offer without hesitation.

"I'm going to become an idol!"

She wanted to be a positive influence on people. And to do that, she needed to put in twice as much effort as she ever had before, working day and night.

Still, she was able to endure it. As long as she had the willpower, she could accomplish anything.

"Can I really keep up with everyone? I'm not being too greedy, right?"

When she finally decided to become both a hunter and an idol, she was genuinely happy that she could do what she loved with the people she cared about.

SysConstStr.WebProb.addtionalopt.descrip:
- Stats granted to main stats will not be granted as bonus stats.
- Already granted bonus stats cannot be duplicated, and new bonus stats are granted with a 1/n chance from the remaining stats, excluding the ones already granted.
- When all 4 bonus stats have been granted and a specific Enhancement Level is reached, the value of 1 of the 4 granted bonus stats will increase. The type of stat that increases is the same with a 1/4 chance.
- If the granted value is a whole number, the value is granted in increments of 1 based on the minimum and maximum guided values, and if the granted value is a percentage, the value is granted in increments of 0.01% based on the minimum and maximum guided values. The rate at which the values are granted is 1/n.
- The rate and value of bonus stats granted in the Artifact Crafting Event are the same as the table below.
- The enhancement and stat values granted during Artifact Modification follow the same rates as the existing Artifact Enhancement Rate.
- Crafting - For some artifacts, you can use Luminous Prism II items during crafting to select up to 2 substats from the available list. The main stat must be selected first during this process. Substats not selected will be randomly granted with a 1/n chance, excluding the selected stat.
(For example, if you select Additional Attack as the main stat of a helmet artifact, one of the remaining 12 stats, excluding Additional Attack, will be granted, with each having a 8.3333% chance of being granted.)

◆ Event Info
- You will obtain one item per draw.
- The number of tickets required for each draw may vary by round.
- Each item can only appear a set number of times until it reaches its limit.
- Certain items become available starting in specific rounds.
- Draw Tickets can be purchased from the linked Special Shop and cannot be used once the draw period ends.
- Some items grant all unclaimed rewards upon acquisition.
- This draw, along with its tickets and items, may return or be sold again in the future.

◆ Rate Info
- Each item is assigned a rate based on its value.
- The rate of each item is calculated based on its ratio of the total value among all available items in the current round.
→ Drop rate for each item = [Value of each item] x [Obtainable quantity] / [Total value of all obtainable items (If multiple items can be obtained, their values are added.)]
- Obtained items are excluded from the pool, and in the next round, rates are readjusted based on the remaining items and their respective values.

Event.2stAnniversary3.Letter.Desc_2:
Hello, hunters. This is SeongKeon Jin, Head of Development for Solo Leveling:ARISE.

As we celebrate our 2nd anniversary, countless moments of growth, laughter, and hardship shared with all of you hunters come to mind.

Now that Sung Jinwoo has reached the Monarch level, these battles may end with a single strike, but none of us have forgotten the desperate fight against Igris in the Job Change Dungeon, or the grueling struggle against Vulcan in the lower floors of the Demons' Castle. As we fought our way through difficult gates and continued striving for more, I find myself once again reflecting deeply on the mindset of E-Rank Sung Jinwoo from those days.

Going forward, we won't be focused solely on pushing out new content. We'll continue to approach the game with the same sense of tension and dedication we had on launch day, doing our utmost to preserve the satisfying action combat and limitless sense of growth that define the core of the experience.

We will not cling solely to the opinions of the development team, but will always take another look from the perspective of our hunters. We promise to remain a development team that always communicates with you and grows together alongside you.

You have been our strongest and most reliable companions until now, we humbly ask that you continue to stand with us on the journey that lies ahead.

Thank you very much!

From SeongKeon Jin, Head of Development for Solo Leveling:ARISE

- You will obtain one item per draw.
- The number of tickets required for each draw may vary by round.

- Each item is assigned a rate based on its value.
- The rate of each item is calculated based on its ratio of the total value among all available items in the current round.

Story.CharacterInfo_13:
Cha Hae-In never had any other aspirations than becoming an athlete. Every day, she regretted the choice she made. "If I was given just one more chance," she thought, "I wouldn't have pushed on and ruined my ankle."

But as she had watched the other runners speed ahead, she couldn't help herself. She felt it from deep down, from her core. She wanted to run. To compete. To not let them win.

But that feeling was all she was left with.

As a result of her injury, she could no longer run like she used to. She grew resentful as her legs didn't move like she wanted, and eventually stopped trying to regain what she had lost.

However, her competitive spirit never completely faded, and eventually led her down a new track.

Standing at the edge of an empty field, she closed her eyes, recalling the times when she was able to run to her heart's content.

In the following silence, she could only feel her ears, her eyes, and her legs.

At the sound of the signal, her legs sped her towards the goal line.

Only when she finally reached it could she hear the world around her again. Even if it was all in her head, she felt satisfied.

Cha Hae-In slowly opened her eyes, crouched down, and corrected her stance. For some odd reason, she felt that she could pull off the perfect run now.

She felt as if a mysterious energy was pumping through her arms, legs, and deep down within her heart. She knew instinctively that she could run like before, and maybe even more, and it would feel good.

She left all of her worries behind and sprinted into the evening breeze. When she looked back, she noticed that her feet had left deep dents in the ground.

It was a sign. Though she could no longer be the athlete that she wanted to be, she was about to start competing on a whole new level.

Story.CharacterInfo_12:
Contrary to her wishes, the public remained interested in her for quite a long time. Cha Hae-In was really uncomfortable being a household name, but fate had other plans.

She was walking on eggshells knowing that every one of her words and actions was examined, as if under a microscope. People even spread false rumors about her.

Even her greatest achievements were stained by the words of anonymous anti-fans.

But Cha Hae-In remained strong.

Her love of running and passion for honest competition kept her going.

Her drive, however, led her to her downfall.

At the end of middle school, Cha Hae-In participated in the first preliminary round of the national student track and field competition. She injured her ankle during the race, but instead of quitting, she decided to press on.

She was able to finish the race, but just barely. To make things worse, she strained her ankle and forced herself to spend more than a year recovering from her injury.

In a way, Cha Hae-In got what she wanted- her fame dissipated as achievements failed materialize. But so did her career as an athlete, as she retired from competing shortly after that.

A cruel fate for someone as passionate as her, all caused by a single mistake.

Story.CharacterInfo_11:
The appearance of mana brought new opportunities for some and despair for others.

For Cha Hae-In, it was both. Her awakening was a once-in-a-lifetime event that brought her both joy and pain.

She had been a promising track and field athlete, on her way to amazing things.

She had a pretty good track record, but even people who weren't interested in track and field knew her name because a video of her competing went viral.

She was more interested in pushing her personal bests than fame, but the public wanted a new star and showered her with attention.

As a young athlete who didn't enjoy being in the limelight, she was embarrassed by this kind of attention.

However, the people around her tried to take advantage of it. People's interest in certain athletic sports can rely heavily on the fame of specific competitors, after all.

While the adults around her pressured her to embrace her newfound fame, she shied away from the cameras and kept to herself, focusing on becoming a better athlete.

What she learned is that attention doesn't make you better at something- and the pressure that comes with it can do the opposite.

It.StringStory.301010045:
The Ghost Candy Bar Where the Soul of the Playful Spirit Sleeps

There was once a boy who longed to visit the amusement park but had no way to pay for a ticket. He wondered "What if I worked there instead?" He soon got a job as a ghost in the Haunted House.

"Boo!"

The boy was so happy when people got scared by his costume. Scaring people was the most fun he had ever had. As time passed, the popularity of the Haunted House died down, and his services were no longer required. The boy was sad, but he found a different job. However, no job could ever make him quite as happy. The boy began to make a made a wish, and kept making that wish until the day he died.

"Please let me scare people again. That's all I want to do for the rest of my life... no, even after I die!"

And sure enough, his wish came true. The boy's soul returned to the amusement park. He hid his soul in a Ghost Candy Bar that looked just like his old costume and waited for the day when he could unleash his frightening visage again.

Story.CharacterInfo_26:
Ever since gates, Dungeons, and monsters became the new normal, the dream job for schoolchildren changed to match. If you asked a random a student on the street what their dream was, most of them would reply "Hunter."

In that regard, Han Song-Yi wasn't all that different from other kids her age. She dreamed of having a spectacular life like the high-ranking Hunters she saw on TV. It was an average dream for an average girl.

Fortunately for her, she was able to take one step closer to becoming a Hunter when she turned 19.

Like the numerous stories she'd read on the Internet, Han Song-Yi suddenly felt a faint power inside her. She immediately went to get evaluated. Even though she received E-Rank, the lowest rank possible, she was still qualified to join Raids.

After that, Han Song-Yi desperately searched for a party that would take her, but of course no one in their right mind would bring an E-Rank high schooler into a Dungeon. Dejected, she turned to the Hunters Association for help, but they also rejected her request, saying that they'd consider her application once she'd graduated.

But she wouldn't give up and she eventually found someone willing to take her on a Raid. However, there was a strange condition: She didn't actually need to go inside the gate, but she'd be paid to just show up and stand outside to fill the headcount requirement. She didn't care, though. Having 19 C-Rank gate clears under her belt would surely help her progress in her Hunter career.

Her confidence surged as she watched Sung Jinwoo, a fellow E-Rank Hunter, complete 19 Raids by himself.

However, after surviving the Red Gate incident, she realized that her confidence was entirely unfounded. Sung Jinwoo didn't clear those gates because he was an E-Rank Hunter; he cleared them because he was Sung Jinwoo.

It.StringStory.301010044:
Pistachio-flavored Candy Bar With Frankenstein's Soul Sleeping Inside

Inside an amusement park, there's an unidentifiable iron gate that leads to a door in the ground. Outside, there's a sign:

"Don't knock without permission!"

The sign sparked countless ghost stories in the minds of passersby. One of the most famous was that behind that door was the body of Dr. Franken, who built an underground bunker to hide from his own horrible creation.

One cloudy day, a mischievous boy knocked on the iron gate.

"Knock, knock."

When nothing happened, the boy quickly lost interest and left. Soon after, the iron gate opened and Dr. Franken's spirit came out. Soon, rumors began to spread that the doctor's spirit had been wandering around the amusement park in search of the boy who woke him up.

Story.CharacterInfo_17:
Yoo Myunghan, chairman of Yoojin Construction, had three children. As the youngest of the three, Yoo Jinho could never measure up to his siblings.

His older brother Jinsung was a genius. He's never gotten less than first place in anything, and led many of his father's projects to glowing praise. His older sister Jinhee was a beloved musical savant.

But Jinho did not share his siblings' talents. No matter how hard he tried to catch up, the result was always the same: his father's disappointment and his brother's condescending laughter.

Yoo Myunghan knew that his company had grown too swiftly to remain stable without constant vigilance. He wanted his company to go to his children, but also knew they needed to be capable of succeeding him.

Not only was Jinho mediocre in academics and art, he was a nervous wreck, despite Myunghan's efforts to raise him otherwise. Myunghan was especially strict in matters that concerned his youngest child.

The result was that Jinho was terrified of failure. He walked on eggshells in his own house to avoid his father's scolding, which only brought him greater scrutiny.

The cycle continued. Jinho's disappointments kept finding their way to his father, and the more his father expressed his disappointment in him, the more Jinho shrank away. Eventually, his father decided to dismiss him entirely.

Despite the sinking feeling that he had let his father down, Jinho was relieved to be able to breathe again. But he wasn't able to enjoy newfound freedom for long.

Without the need to prove himself, he was left to drift aimlessly. One day, while jealously watching his siblings shine at a family gathering, Jinho finally found his purpose.

He needed to do something big. Not for his father, but for him. He wanted to show up his siblings just once, regardless of whether it pleased his father or not.

As if the heavens themselves had heard his prayer, something big did, in fact, appear: the world was suddenly rocked by gates, mana, and awakened beings. And Jinho was the only one in his family to become one.

He didn't get a high rank, but now, he had a clear path.

He spent countless hours planning and preparing, and finally walked into his father's office to confront his biggest fear.

He handed his father the paperwork showing that he was qualified to be a Guild Master and demanded that Yoojin Construction create a guild and make him the guild master.

And thus, despite the odds, Jinho had caught his father's eye once again.

Story.CharacterInfo_27:
Despite wielding fire magic on a daily basis, Choi Jong-In is uncomfortable around fire. Over the course of his life, many of his greatest misfortunes involved fire.

For example, his house once caught on fire due to a minor mistake in the electrical wiring, his office was nearly destroyed by a fire that had spread from the neighboring store, and he almost lost an eye when a firecracker misfired directly into his face.

Although fire had caused him to suffer time and time again, he'd thought nothing of it and believed that his incendiary misfortunes were just part of the average trials and tribulations of life.

Incomprehensible things happened every day, after all. He had his hands so full trying to keep up with these constant dramatic changes, that he was never able to spend much time dwelling on his past troubles.

He'd rather use his time to do something productive. Change leads to opportunity, and monumental changes were happening all the time. To him, there was no reason to examine the past instead of thinking of a way forward.

Choi Jong-In works tirelessly to improve his life and the lives of those around him, blissfully unaware that he is actually playing with fire.

Story.CharacterInfo_16:
Some believe evil is innate. You'll find no evidence more convincing than Kang Taeshik. Even as a child, he would delight in tormenting insects and small animals.

He would systematically brutalize the creatures, then respectfully lay them to rest. He started conducting a ceremony before he began his remorseless torture as well, until this ritual evolved into something he found sacred.

Taeshik was clever enough to never get caught. In front of others, he was a model student and upright citizen. No one suspected that he could have been hiding anything.

Every time he saw a character like him in popular culture, he would privately laugh to himself. They were all given some sort of tragic backstory or a web of complex motivations.

He had no such motivations. There was no special reason behind his cruelty. He was merely entertained by the cries of fear from his victims as they hopelessly struggled in the face of their imminent death.

Eventually, he would get bored of tormenting one particular sort of creature and would set out in search of others. He was always searching for a new victim, getting bored of them faster each time. As he ran out of stimuli, large swaths of time began to pass without holding any meaning to him.

He needed... something stronger.

And he knew what it was: the most dangerous prey. Humans.

He set out in search of a victim.

But when he finally closed in on his selected target...

They were whisked away into a cerulean vortex, right before his very eyes.

He immediately thought of the "blue portals" he had heard about on the news.

Only the chosen could enter, and those who did not return swiftly were lost forever.

Curious, he took a tentative step forward. Their exclusivity had been greatly exaggerated: he easily slipped into the gate.

There, he saw his target fighting off a horde of monsters. Though his frightened target's movements were clumsy, the monsters were steadily decreasing in number.

It was only after the fight had ended that his target noticed he had arrived. Kang Taeshik put on his best "helpless civilian" act and approached.

As his bewildered target started to question him, Taeshik drove a dagger into his target's body and watched them crumple.

"This is the perfect place for me," he thought, methodically twisting the knife in his fallen target. 

When he left the gate, he blended into the crowd, hiding the possessions he'd swiped, including a shiny rock inscribed with a strange pattern.

Four years later, Taeshik's skill with a knife got him hired at the Hunters Association.

He gained respect for his eagerness to go out into the field, and no one questioned the reason why the survival rate of raids he'd been involved with was so low.

Thus, he was able to continue his "hunter-hunting" habit... at least, until he ran into Sung Jinwoo.

Story.CharacterInfo.Desc261.01.06: After it became known that Yoo Soohyun was an A-Rank hunter, this was the title of the first article about it. She would blush and say it was embarrassing to hear, but in her heart, she knew it was true. With her looks, she scored work as a child actor and continued to excel as an adult by becoming a model. As her net worth was rising, her wealthy upbringing sparked further public interest.
Story.CharacterInfo_24:
Everyone has dreamed about winning the lottery at least once in their life. Jo Kyuhwan certainly had. He would watch the S-Rank hunters on television, and dream of what his life could be if he were like them.

He knew that awakening wasn't something he could just will into existence. He also knew that becoming a high-ranked Hunter was astronomically rare.

That's why, instead of expecting the moon, he aimed for the stars.

Becoming a B-Rank Hunter would be enough to lead a pretty good life. A-Rank is pretty high, and he wouldn't even dream of becoming an S-Rank.

And so he thought his dreams were realistic. He thought that he really could awaken as a B-Rank Hunter. Unfortunately, reality had other ideas.

He was a C-Rank Mage-type awakened being.

Compared to the number of Physical-type Hunters out there, Mage and Support-type hunters were certainly more rare and desirable. If he worked hard and improved himself, he might have even had a chance of joining a major guild.

But among hunters, ranks are absolute. Even if he were to join a major guild, it was highly unlikely that he would make a bigger splash than the hunters who ranked higher than him.

He was beyond disappointed. He thought that it was all unfair. He'd finally had his awakening, but he'd never get the chance to live the easy life that he'd dreamed of.

Didn't he deserve it? There was no point in risking his life every day for the relatively low pay of a C-Rank hunter. He began searching for other ways to make money with his power.

Instead of joining a guild, he sought... alternative methods.

His chance encounter with Hwang Dongsuk was all that he needed to enter that line of business. He quickly became Dongsuk's right-hand man, in charge of seeking out the "bait" to accompany them on their expeditions.

Story.CharacterInfo_15:
"Wait... that bridge looks like it's going to collapse."

The Guild was conducting a mock raid for newly admitted hunters at their training grounds. No real monsters were involved, of course. The goal was to safely find the way out of the mock-dungeon.

Park Heejin was torn about whether to tell the other newbies about the bridge.

The training grounds were faithfully modeled after the inside of a dungeon, and the hunters were faced with a shallow ravine. There was a sign warning them about a much deeper fall, and an old bridge leading to the other side.

When her fellow hunters cautiously started to cross, Heejin noticed something give, ever so slightly. She refused to join them.

She knew that her fellow hunters were desperate to get bonus points for the safe return of all hunters in their group, so she figured they wouldn't leave her if she decided not to cross.

This left them at an impasse.

Even as a little child, Heejin's intuition was remarkably good.

She noticed even the slightest of changes in the environment, and nearly every time she thought something bad was going to happen, it did.

But though her intuition was good, it wasn't perfect.

Only of few of the people she told the people around her about her premonitions took action and avoided the coming disaster. Some people didn't change their behavior at all and turned out just fine.

So, afraid of judgment, Heejin tended to keep her predictions to herself.

This was one of those times.

Even as her fellow hunters yelled at her to cross, she stood in silent hesitation.

Unfortunately, without a good explanation for her behavior, the other hunters decided to leave without her, forfeiting the bonus points. When they reached the center of the bridge, it gave way with a loud cracking sound.

The group grumbled and got back up on their feet as they were handed a failing score by the test administrators, who had marked them as "dead."

Heejin, on the other hand, received flying colors for being the only one left alive. That hadn't been her intention.

By passing the test, she was given the opportunity to attend practical training and official raids, but had earned the ire of her angry teammates from the exam. There was nothing that she could really say.

How could she have explained her scarily correct premonition? She couldn't trust her own instincts, and neither would they.

An incident on a snowy mountain changed her mind about her premonitions.

She was chased out of a Dungeon with her tail between her legs, unable to retrieve the corpses of the people she'd been training with... If only she had trusted herself. That was not an experience that she would like to ever have again.

Story.CharacterInfo_25:
Misery was Hwang Dongsuk's childhood companion.

When he was fifteen, his parents died in a car accident, and he and his brother were left in the care of their grandmother, who died of a chronic illness soon thereafter.

He saw the negligent driver that killed his parents get off with a warning. The driver never even apologized to the two young boys of the family they destroyed.

Caring for Dongsuk and Dongsoo caused their grandmother to neglect her own illness, expediting her death.

By this point, Dongsuk knew that his family's poverty was at the root of it all.

As he put on a black tie for the second time to stand alone at an empty funeral, he asked himself why the whole sorry chain of events had been set into motion. The questions didn't stop, and eventually, he grew to blame the world itself.

Then, he went after revenge. His brother Dongsoo readily followed his lead as they dove into a life of crime.

Dongsuk had a never-ending list of ideas for ways to make a killing, and Dongsoo would always faithfully carry them out.

Each time things went as planned, they would try to make the next job even bigger. They swindled countless people out of their money and left them saddled with debt.

But a life of crime comes with its consequences. Dongsuk spent a lot of time going in and out of jail. But he never repented or even questioned himself- not when his victims broke down into tears in front of him, nor when they howled bloody murder about how deeply he had hurt them.

They suffered because they were weak. They were stupid, poor, and powerless to stop him.

That's how the world was meant to be. That was how the world treated him. He had no intention of obeying the rules of a society that so thoroughly abandoned him and his brother. Society isn't designed to protect the weak. In order to survive, you must take from others what you need.

His was a twisted philosophy, but there was no one capable of correcting his course, so there was no way out of the shady path he had forged for himself.

Then, a new stage for crime presented itself.

The gates had appeared.

Hwang Dongsuk knew an opportunity when he saw one.

Even before becoming an awakened being, he'd been convicted of fraud several times for claiming insurance money for fake magic beast run-ins, holding "awakening classes" for children while masquerading as the Hunters Association, and many more gate-related schemes.

After becoming an awakened being, he would regularly bring "bait" onto a Raid and treat the hired hunters like disposable tools.

But crime never pays. Hwang Dongsuk spent a lifetime drinking in his victims' tears but didn't have a chance to shed his own before he was unceremoniously slain in turn by one of those would-be victims.

An unremarkable end for an unremarkable villain.

Story.CharacterInfo_14:
Kim Chul never failed.

He was a born athlete, naturally fast and strong. Before he became a hunter, he had tried many sports, but quickly lost interest in every one.

The reason was simple.

It was all too easy. Though he never played a sport for long, it was long enough for him to gauge his own talent and potential.

Everyone constantly told him, "If you take on the right training regimen, you're going to make a name for yourself as an athlete." That was all he needed to hear. He decided that it was inevitable: he was going to be an athletic star.

After trying out different sports, he chose to pursue track and field. After all, there was no better sport than to push the raw physical limits of the human body. And, as expected, he rocketed to the top.

During his races, he would often look back at the "losers" behind him and think to himself:

"There's a clear and unmistakable gap in talent.

They're all morons to keep competing against someone with such an overwhelming advantage."

Basking in his "God-given talent," Chul quit track and field shortly afterwards, satisfied with his dominating performance.

He needed a greater challenge. One that would garner him even more praise and recognition.

He once again drifted from sport to sport, but he had a hard time finding that challenge. Life was boring, and none of the praise he received satisfied him anymore.

As life would have it, the greater challenge he was seeking finally arrived with the gates. He wasn't the strongest awakened being known to man, but he was deemed to be capable of becoming an A-Rank Hunter.

Hunter training was beyond boring. He wanted nothing more than to join raids right away, but his guild talked him down and convinced him to follow the proper process of becoming a hunter.

They told him that once he properly learned the ropes, he would be in charge of leading multiple raids. He would become famous, just like the S-Rank hunters.

All of it went straight to his head. He thought about Park Jongsoo, another A-Rank hunter who led his own a major guild, despite not being an S-Rank hunter. With his training complete and his dreams of glory dancing in his mind, Kim Chul entered the C-Rank gate for some practical combat training.

Inside, however, all that was waiting for him were biting winds blowing over a snowy plain... and Ice Elves, better known by their moniker "of Ice Slayers".

Story.CharacterInfo_22:
Lee Joohee was still in high school when she became an awakened being.

Four years ago, during a record-breaking July heatwave, she was taking one of her daily walks.

She would visit the same place in the countryside on vacation every year, so she knew her route like the back of her hand.

A slow, leisurely walk did wonders to clear her head. Admiring the familiar but beautiful scenery pushed her worries to the back of her mind, and finding tiny changes in her surroundings out on her walk gave her hope: since things were always changing, all of her problems would eventually go away as well.

That's why she loved her countryside walks.

But for some reason, on that particular day, she felt compelled to stray from her regular path, as if she were being guided by an inexplicable force. She walked deeper and deeper into the forest.

There, she discovered something that could not be described as a "tiny change." Between the trees, behind the undergrowth, she found a swirling blue light.

She'd heard about the so-called "gates" before on the evening news. This one was no bigger than the ones she'd seen in pictures, but she instinctively knew that it was trouble.

With shaking hands, she dialed the Hunters Association's number and reported the gate, snapping a picture as proof. But the words of an article that she'd read a couple of days before entered her mind.

It had said that gates that appeared out in the countryside were often pushed down on the priority list and tended to not be closed fast enough, causing "Dungeon Breaks" that could devastate rural communities.

Until the hunters arrived to close the gate, she needed to warn the few townsfolk and get them to evacuate.

She knew next to nothing about hunters and gates, but the fact that no regular person stood a chance against the monsters inside was common knowledge. She quickly hurried back to spread the word.

Everyone began quickly packing their things and getting ready to leave. Ever since the Jeju Island Raid disaster was broadcast on national television, there wasn't a soul that didn't know that monsters meant danger.

She made sure to spread the word to everyone, from the people working the fields, to those who had gone to visit a neighboring town.

Only after everyone had gotten ready to leave was she finally able to return to her grandmother's house. Her grandmother was away, so she hurriedly packed all of their things... but suddenly, she was hit with a sinking feeling.

She hadn't seen her little cousin all day. Not at home, nor on the streets. She remembered that her cousin had skipped breakfast to leave early that morning to go catch fish with the neighborhood kids. She couldn't find them at the nearby creek or the paddies.

She racked her brain to think of where else they may have gone fishing, and remembered that she had heard the sound of running water on her walk... close to where she had found the gate.

She shuddered to think of what might become of the children if monsters emerged.

Worries swirling in her mind, she ran back to the gate.

Unfortunately, she was right to worry.

A Werewolf stood at the gate entrance, looking around for something.

She quickly hid behind a tree and tried to think.

Would she be able to get to the creek without being caught? If she reported the Dungeon Break to the Hunters Association, how soon could they arrive?

The harder she thought, the less clear everything was.

She felt the time passing as she sat frozen, paralyzed by indecision. While she was staring at the Hunters Association's number in her phone when a scream broke her out of her daze.

The Werewolf was gone, and she could see large paw prints leading towards the creek.

She tried to keep her fears at bay while she crept towards the creek as quietly as she could. There, she found the bodies of the children. She could see her little cousin's head poking out from between two boulders.

The Werewolf was long gone, having lost interest in the scene.

She raced towards the boulders. Her cousin was gasping for air.

She didn't know where to begin with treatment, but when she put her hand over her cousin's wounds, they began to close up.

But she could feel her little cousin growing weaker.

Lying by a creek near a gate was no place for a small child to be, let alone a wounded one. She needed to get her cousin away from this place and get some real help.

She stopped treating the wounds, threw her cousin over her shoulder, and ran down back out of the forest as fast as she could.

She didn't remember a lot after that... save for the armed hunters and Hunters Association staff standing over the beheaded Werewolf.

As soon as they saw her, they rushed over to help. But when she saw the stony faces of the hunters, her heart sank.

Maybe she should've known when she had felt her cousin's breath stop. No... she had known, but did not want to accept what had happened.

She blamed herself. She had failed her cousin. She had made the wrong choices.

The hunters tried their best to console her. They told her that she had done everything right. That they were only able to arrive quickly because they had been out in the area on a mission, and everything could have been much worse. But in that moment, none of that mattered to her.

When the situation was resolved and she went in to give her report about it, she was determined to embrace her power as an awakened being. But she couldn't take the leap and become a hunter. She didn't feel she even had the right to use her powers at all.

Until Woo Jinchul personally went to persuade her three years later, she left her powers buried along with her past, by that creek where it all started.

Story.CharacterInfo_23:
Low-ranking gates appear more frequently than their high-ranking counterparts. As a result, simply by a matter of numbers, low-ranking gates are the source of most Dungeon Breaks.

In one particular neighborhood, a D-Rank gate was not dealt with for a full week, despite the residents' numerous protests.

Hunters only arrived at the scene after the fact, and their teamwork was awkward at best and disastrous at worst.

Certainly, they were able to cull the monsters, but the hunters were pulled together at the last minute, and they had made several noticeable mistakes.

After the boss was killed, the gate closed, and the hunters' crew off to the next location, the residents were finally able to breathe a sigh of relief and return to their homes.

Song Chiyul and his family were among those residents. He had asked the Hunters Association staff if they had done a sweep to make sure the area was completely safe and didn't receive a straight answer, but with the gate closed, he thought nothing of it.

He was assured that D-Rank dungeons had only weaker monsters, and the hunters on the scene were very experienced.

But something was still bothering him. To put his mind to rest, he did his own sweep of his house, checking every room... a decision he regrets to this day.

While he was inside, he heard screams coming from his front yard. He quickly grabbed his wooden sword and ran outside.

His children lay still in the grass while a group of goblins targeted his wife.

He knew in his head that ordinary people weren't a match for even the weakest of monsters, but he had no time to consider other options.

Wooden sword in hand, he rushed the Goblins.

He was confident in his swordsmanship.

He had competed in international kendo tournaments. He had won medals and trophies. He thought he could take down a couple of small Goblins.

He was wrong.

No matter how many hits he landed against the Goblins, they shrugged them all off. They slowly but surely landed blow after blow against him, until one of them finally brought him down to his knees.

By this point, his wife had fallen silent. He instinctively knew that it was the end of the road for him as well.

He tried to force his body to move, to lead them inside and burn down the house, just so that the Goblins would not escape to attack another family.

Then, just as their teeth were about to close in on his neck, an arrow pierced one of the Goblin's skulls.

Through hazy vision, he looked up to see a woman running to his aid, striking down the Goblins one by one.

This was the last thing he saw before he woke up at the hospital. He was immediately bombarded with questions from all sorts of media outlets wanting to run his story, with or without his input.

Soon after, the hunters and Hunters Association staff involved with the raid came to him with their heads bowed. Some of them even came back and visited him every day. At first, he could not bring himself to forgive them. He threw whatever he could get his hands on at them in fits of rage, but eventually, his anger ebbed and he began to focus his energies on the more fundamental issues.

The major guilds only wanted to use their manpower and resources to clear the high-ranking dungeons for profit. And the Hunters Association who handled most of the low-ranked dungeons were bleeding members. After all, who would want to do more dangerous work for lower pay?

The problem was the lack of resources and manpower to ensure that tragedies like this wouldn't happen over and over again.

How could one man be able to stop it? What could he possibly do?

He had his answer before long.

One fateful day, Song Chiyul's powers awoke. Oddly enough, though he had spent his entire life devoted to the sword, he developed a gift for spellcasting. Regardless, he welcomed any power that would help him achieve his goals.

As a mage, he was sought out by many decently-sized guilds, but he turned down every one and instead elected to form a neighborhood watch, with hunters who had survived similar experiences and had refused to join the guilds.

They would be the ones to work with the Hunters Association to close the lower-rank gates. And they would be sure not to make any mistakes.

It.StringStory.301010043:
Grape-flavored Candy Bar With a Vampire's Soul Sleeping Inside

It was the dead of night. Darkness engulfed the city and a strange noise came from the warehouse at the entrance of an amusement park. It was loud, but the amusement park was dark and no one was there to hear it.

"Rattle, rattle..."

The repetitive noise was soon ended by a loud BANG as a diamond-shaped antique coffin popped open. It had been purchased long ago to be used as a prop... but what came out from the coffin was a man as skinny as a skeleton.

"Th- thirsty..."

The man dragged his heavy body out the warehouse doors.

"Blood...!"

Exhausted and dehydrated, he discovered a dark red liquid inside a food truck and gulped it down. But what he thought was blood was actually... homemade grape syrup. His body hardened and turned to powder, falling into the goo. Soon enough, a little girl was eating him as a sweet snack.

Story.CharacterInfo_20:
His outlook on life only started to change when the gates appeared.

Even though he couldn't explain why or how, he was able to sense and harness the "mana" flowing around him.

At first, he thought that anyone could learn to use it, but he soon realized just how special his power was.

He saw his newfound abilities as a curse. Now that he was capable of things beyond the power of an ordinary human, he could no longer enjoy his tennis matches.

What fun is there in playing a game where the victor is always decided? His powers made it impossible for him to follow the core tenant of sportsmanship: fair play.

Robbed of his sole source of enjoyment in life, he looked elsewhere for meaning. Preferably in something where his newfound power would not get in his way.

He learned that others like him were using their awakened powers to fight the mysterious monsters that had been emerging from the gates.

The media called them heroes. Despite the ever-increasing number of casualties, the praise for these "hunters" never faltered.

Tae-Gyu had found his new calling. If he was forced off the path of sports by his power, then he just needed to wield his newfound power to forge a new path for himself.

Filled with determination, he stepped on to his first battlefield and immediately felt that he had been right.

Fighting monsters was just as enjoyable as hitting a striped yellow ball past the other player. He could do this all day.

Story.CharacterInfo_19:
No amount of talent can beat hard work, but no amount of hard work can beat someone who enjoys doing it for a living.

This was Lim Tae-Gyu's mantra.

He wasn't the most talented player, but he enjoyed tennis more than anyone else.

His passion bolstered his talent and inspired him to excel: regardless of who his opponent was, in order to fully enjoy the match, he had to possess skills to compete with them.

Every time he stepped out on to the court, he was calm and composed. He was happy to just to play. What did he have to worry about?

Some mistook his demeanor for arrogance, but Tae-Gyu never really thought much of it. He wasn't really interested in clearing up those misunderstandings.

He was only interested in playing, and he would be satisfied with the result, no matter what it was. As an athlete, these were the only two things that really mattered to him.

Story.CharacterInfo_21:
In the days before the hunter scene had any structure, any particularly strong hunter could garner media attention and become an overnight celebrity.

Lim Tae-Gyu was one such hunter.

His arrows always landed between the eyes of his enemies, and no magic beast would survive venturing within the range of his bow.

The rumors grew out of control: it was said that a single one of his arrows could kill ten magic beasts, and he did his best to live up to the public's expectations.

Of course, he never abandoned his theory that talent and hard work could never beat enjoyment.

Repeatedly facing the unpredictable trajectory of a tennis ball had been the perfect training tool for the ever-changing, chaotic nature of the battlefield.

He even felt that the more chaotic the situation was, the more fun it would be.

Even as he founded and led a monolithic guild with his comrades-in-arms, and even as he was called to Jeju Island to deal with the first S-Rank gate, he never forgot to have fun.

But the Jeju Island raid killed many of his dear teammates. Suddenly, he was forced to confront the sobering truth.

Fighting results in death. And death isn't fun.

The monsters they faced weren't playing a game. They were intelligent, brutal beings that cared about nothing outside of killing hunters. No amount of preparation or training could truly protect you against them; because they didn't care about playing fair.

One moment of hesitation or the slightest mistake was all it took. And when you lose to monsters, there are no rematches. You never get to play again.

The fact that his failure to grasp such a simple concept cost him the lives of his closest comrades tormented him. But regrets do not bring back the dead. These days, Tae-Gyu steps onto the battlefield with a new resolve.

Fighting is no longer a game to him. There is no more fun. And if he forgets, it is the voices of his dead friends that he hears reminding him:

It matters if you win or lose.

It.StringStory.302030034_IDLE1:
On her way to school, a girl who dreamed of becoming a star faced a city swallowed by magic beasts. The dungeon break had forced her into a life-or-death situation: a magic beast's grip tightened around her neck.

"I want to become an idol. I don't want to die like this!"

In that moment, the girl's untamed spirit stirred inside her. That spirit bestowed upon her a unique power, which she used to save herself.

As time passed, the girl fulfilled her wish and became a star. Beloved by countless fans, that awakened power still lived within her, waiting to blossom again. 

"I'll use this power to protect the ones I cherish."

That resolve grew clearer under the moonlight. The moon itself seemed to hear her promise and quietly pushed her forward.

Story.CharacterInfo_18:
No one can believe that Baek Yoonho was a selfless firefighter before he became a hunter.

His exceptionally large physique and menacing looks give off the impression that could defeat any Magic Beast with one hand behind his back.

Even before the gates appeared, Yoonho was aware that people were nice to him out of fear. But he has always worked hard to make himself genuinely worthy of their respect.

Despite his efforts, however, one year after the first gate opened, he faced some not-so-welcome changes.

The first was that his mentor, who had become a hunter, vanished inside a dungeon when the gate closed.

When he saw the story on the news, he couldn't bring himself to be upset. After all, the reasons he respected the man were the same reasons why his mentor had allowed himself to be sacrificed for the sake of others.

The second was that he himself awakened with formidable powers. He gained his Beast Transformation ability, which allowed him to take a shape similar to the monsters in order to fight them. In other words, to become a monster. He hated the power.

However, he couldn't just stand by while civilians were in danger, so he joined the fight and cleared as many dungeons as he could. But people didn't even bother to look at him kindly anymore.

He understood their reasons- people were afraid of the shape he took and the powers he could wield. But that didn't mean it didn't depress him. After two years, things continued to evolve: Yoonho was able to fully control his powers, and both the United States and Korea adopted the same hunter-ranking system.

He was classified as an S-Rank, and the public once again began to look upon him with favor. He no longer had to worry about being mistaken for a Magic Beast. 

In his third year, Lim Tae-Gyu, who had already made a reputation for himself, gathered Yoonho and two other S-Rank hunters to establish Korea's first major guild, the Fiend Guild.

Baek Yoonho worked tirelessly to ensure the guild's growth.

However, he soon began to clash with Tae-Gyu. Tae-Gyu wanted to expand the guild, and Yoonho wanted the guild members to receive a bigger profit share. In the end, when they couldn't come to an agreement, Baek Yoonho took the members that sided with him and established a new guild: the White Tiger Guild.

Things went smoothly after that.

No one dared question Yoonho or his beastly scowl, and the guild grew

Even so, Yoonho tried not to use his Beast Transformation very often. He knew how people viewed both his natural appearance and his ability, and he was eager to avoid their unwanted judgment.

As a result, it became an urban legend that his beast form was an unofficial indicator of disaster.

They say, if Baek Yoonho is ever forced to fully transform, that can only mean a tremendously powerful magic beast is nearby, so it's a good time to run!

Story.CharacterInfo_31:
Although fire is the most common type of magic for Mage-type Hunters, its effects vary dramatically depending on the individual Hunter.

Choi Jong-In's examination results put him in S-Rank, the rank granted to hunters with immeasurable power. Essentially, he possessed enough firepower to clear a B-Rank gate by himself.

Of course, he didn't know that, or he wouldn't have tested his abilities and nearly burned down a whole building

Both the fact that he set the building ablaze, yet it didn't collapse were both due to his inability to control his mana power.

It was all very ironic.

The flames which had set him back at key moments in his life had now become second nature as his unique ability and brought more success than ever before as the strongest hunter in Korea.

He had a lingering suspicion that a hunter's abilities were determined by their traumatic memories or their greatest regrets.

If true, it meant that every time a hunter faced off against a monster, they would fight out of desperation, not duty, to make sure their worst moments weren't repeated.

As smart and perceptive as Choi Jong-In was, he was also good at pushing away whatever he deemed to be unimportant. This was no time to be sentimental.

Regardless of how he obtained his power, this was the opportunity he'd been waiting for. In fact, it was the mother of all opportunities. Even if his awakening were caused by past misfortunes, he was determined to not make them the defining feature of his future.

Awakening or not, that side of him hadn't changed. He had to move forward.

To that end, he considered leveraging the fame and power of his 'S-Rank Hunter' status to be the best course of action.

Staring at the Guild Master certification and the veritable mountain of business cards on his desk, he fell into deep thought.

Story.CharacterInfo_30:
The definition of an Awakened Being is a person that can sense Mana and manipulate it to affect their surroundings. Before long, they will instinctively feel and wield their abilities.

If this was true, then Choi Jong-In instinctively felt like he could cause that large explosion he so desperately needed right now.

The crossroads of life and death finally forced the workaholic to focus on his own body. He felt a new mysterious power within him, and it was close to bursting out through his fingers.

The cigarette he lit as his last no longer felt like a candle mourning the soon-to-be deceased, but rather the fuse of an immense bomb.

And it was going to blow any second. There was nothing left for him to do but throw it at the monster staring him down.

He watched as the small flame arced in the air and landed perfectly on the Golem's head. The ground shook as a deafening explosion followed. The Golem's hand, just inches over his head, crumbled to ash.

After the first attack, something clicked. More explosions soon followed, and the Golems that were a safe distance away from the other civilians also turned to dust.

The noise drew the attention of the other Golems, luring them away from the others and into Choi Jong-In's deadly flames. He set off an even greater explosion near the center of the Golems, and they crumbled before him.

He couldn't control the power of the explosions as well as he'd like, but he did good enough for his first fight.

To the people he saved, it wasn't just good enough, it was beyond belief. The stories spread about that day eventually evolved to create his moniker as "The Strongest Hunter of All Mankind."

Story.CharacterInfo_33:
In the bygone era of nine years ago, when the contents of the gates were still unknown...

Hunters fought the monsters not for profit, but to protect others.

As a college student, Woo Jinchul did not care much about Dungeons and Hunters, no matter how frequently they were on the news.

He was determined to become an officer of the law and bring evildoers to justice. It was his lifelong dream, and his only motivation.

Even if the world changed, and people suffered more at the hands of the monsters than human criminals, his determination never faltered.

But there was one story on the news that changed him.

It was a live broadcast of a horrific scene, inside a now-joyless amusement park. There were Hunters laying on the ground, moaning in pain, and people everywhere, running around aimlessly, screaming for help.

The last shot of the broadcast was oddly calm. It showed a boy, staring glassy-eyed at a now-closed gate.

Woo Jinchul later learned that the boy was the son of a Hunter who had gone in to rescue other Hunters, but was the only one to not make it back.

The lost Hunter was quite famous. Even someone as uninterested in the news as Woo Jinchul knew his name.

It was meant to be an uplifting story: The Hunters saved the day yet again, suffering casualties but ultimately driving back the monsters that poured from the gate. But all Woo Jinchul saw was the sacrifices made that day, and a boy who'd lost his father.

He thought long and hard about it. The reason why he wanted to become an officer of the law was not because of petty fascination or admiration. He wanted to save the unfortunate from the evils of others.

But while he watched the scenes from the amusement park, only one question was going through his head: Hunters put their lives on the lines to protect the people, but who protects the Hunters?

There was news that Hunters were forming Guilds to better handle Dungeons, but there was never any news about protections or services offered to Hunters.

As he learned more and more about the subject, he was filled with a strong desire to protect the unprotected, to right the wrong that society expected so much from Hunters yet provided them with so little. When he heard the news that Go Gunhee, a business owner turned Hunter, was forming a Hunters Association modeled after the USA's Federal Bureau of Hunters, he knew what he had to do.

He studied hard so he could work for the Hunters Association. Unfortunately for him, his Awakening made most of his efforts worthless, but he wasn't too bothered by it because he wanted to be in the field as much as possible.

Finally, the day came. He stood in front of Go Gunhee as a new employee, and told him about his dream, confident that it was the first step to making it a reality.

But dreams never really come true. He would learn that the hard way.

Story.CharacterInfo_28:
Just as Choi Jong-In predicted, the dramatic changes to the world did bring about new business opportunities.

Raw Mana Crystals and Essence Stones could be turned into building materials that sold for unbelievable amounts. Also, by being out in the field and completing transaction after transaction, he could build himself up as a trustworthy figure.

He knew very well that networking was the key to success. Networking brought him information, and in this chaotic world, information brought him power... and money.

His unfortunate run-ins with fire, or any other worry of his, could not hold a candle to his new, lucrative career. He didn't notice the gradual changes happening to his own body.

It was only brought to his attention when a figurative knife was held up to his throat.

In his line of work, fieldwork meant danger.

But six years is a long, long time - long enough for even the greatest of dangers to become familiar. The field was dominated by recklessness, a far cry from the constant alertness required in life-or-death situations.

It was an unfortunate side-effect of humanity's incredible adaptability. Even if danger was constantly staring them down, people in field were so used to it that they could overlook it.

Everyone else turned a blind eye to the ongoing backroom deals.

Reporters would often pay local crews a small fee to get closer to the scene, sometimes within containment zones.

Traders and merchants like Choi Jong-In would also come to these sites with cash in unmarked envelopes. The operation he supervised was routine: Prepare to process the Magic Beast corpses left behind by a smaller Guild.

But the negligent atmosphere and lack of Hunters turned what would have been a small incident into a full-blown disaster. The gate should have been dormant for a couple more days, but monsters started pouring out one after another, and the situation outside devolved into chaos.
Dialog.Group1804012-011: (Looks like he couldn't get away due to his injuries.)
Story.CharacterInfo_32:
After the incident four years ago, instead of quitting his life as a hunter, Kim Sangshik made two rules to live by.

Rule one: Stay away from danger. Rule two: Prioritize survival over earnings.

However, as with all things, the memory of that incident grew hazy, and his resolve faded over time.

As he stood on the final altar after surviving the Cartenon Temple, he suddenly remembered those two rules he'd made four years ago.

In order to keep his family alive, he had to survive at all costs. He couldn't leave his wife and children behind.

Why did he only remember his rules now? Despite mumbling the rules to himself out of habit upon entering the gate, why didn't he follow his own advice? Even though waves of regret washed over him, he wasn't about to turn a blind eye to reality. He had entrusted his life to the wild plan thought up by the Weakest Hunter of All Mankind.

As he watched two more hunters abandon hope and make a run for it, and the doors gradually close behind them, a typhoon of worries formed in his mind.

No matter what happened, he had to survive. For his wife. For his kids. But if he ran away like those two did, the rest of the party would surely face a tragic end in the temple.

The memory of that day four years ago cut into him like a knife. He barely survived, shielded by another hunter. He knew it was wrong, but crying bitter tears of both regret and repentance, he chose to flee once more.

Such a choice was only hard the first time.

Later, when he faced the survivors that he had again abandoned, he had a nagging feeling that karma was coming for him.

He felt that he was about to pay for the unforgivable things that he'd done.

He thought that bowing his head to Jinwoo would be the first step towards righting his wrongs. But fate is cruel. He was destined to become the honest hunter he longed to be, but only in death.

He met his end at the hands of a murderous hunter inside a Dungeon, just like the incident that redefined his life so long ago.

Story.CharacterInfo_29:
Even in today's world, there's no guarantee that every gate created can be found in time.

Although the number of people who could sense Mana grew, transporting them to remote locations still remained a challenging task.

Because of this, gates found in rural areas tended to only get cleared 2 to 3 days after discovery.

This gate was handled within that time frame as well, but it had unfortunately appeared much earlier and was discovered too late.

That was an inherent risk in entering gates in remote areas.
Anyone entering one would have been trained to deal with a sudden Dungeon Break.

However, there was no veteran Hunter on the scene to take control of this situation. The Hunters Association representative in charge of the operation was the first to flee. There was no hope of an organized response.

Those remaining were left to face a C-Rank gate alone.
The Raid team was comprised of eight Hunters from a small Guild and two low-rank Hunters who were recruited to fill the minimum headcount.

It shouldn't have been a difficult Dungeon for them, but even as a swarm of large cobalt Golems came charging through the gate, no Hunter followed.

At this point, it was clear that the Raid team had missed an area that they should've cleared out, or everyone was dead.

Choi Jong-In had the presence of mind to immediately find a hiding place, and racked his brain for a way out while also trying his hardest to ignore the harrowing screams all around him.

The gate had spawned inside a shallow cave, so there was only one exit.

He prayed that the Golems would be witless enough to break down the cave walls with their attacks, creating more escape routes.

But that was wishful thinking. He needed a more surefire method if he was to survive.

Perhaps if there was some kind of large explosion to distract the Golems, he could make a run for it.

What object could cause such an explosion...?
He scanned his surroundings for anything that fit that description.

But explosives had no effect on the monsters within the Dungeons, so there was no reason for any to be there. Realization spread over him like a dark cloud.

This was the end. There was no hope.

Story.CharacterInfo_35:
Hwang Dongsoo was the eighth S-Rank hunter born in South Korea. He left Korea to join the Scavenger Guild in America.

When he left, he was criticized for "forsaking his country," but he didn't care.

He responded, "Since I became an S-Rank hunter, I haven't gotten anything from the Hunters Association except their rancid breath on my neck."

However, the Hunters Association's wasn't keeping a close watch because he was an "S-Rank hunter," it was because he and his brother had a nasty reputation.

Dongsoo and Dongsuk had extensive criminal records for violence and theft. And since they had gained powers, ordinary humans were no match for them. The Association suspected that instead of using their gifts for killing monsters, the brothers were up to their old tricks.

Upset with the Hunters Association's accusations, Dongsoo had no qualms about moving to the USA.

When he left for the States, he asked his brother to come with him, but Hwang Dongsuk declined.

At least, that's how the story goes.

The two brothers seemed to have a strong bond. Since they had always worked together, people were surprised by Hwang Dongsuk's decision.

Though their brotherly bond looked perfect on the outside, on the inside, there was no loyalty.

Dongsoo had always been in his brother's shadow. Dongsuk was the only one that ever received praise.

Even when their parents' death started to lead Dongsuk down a dangerous path, Dongsoo couldn't escape the need to outdo him.

Wanting to be better than his brother drove him to commit acts of worse and worse nature. After all, the two brothers considered their rap sheets a list of achievements.

Even when the gates appeared and the power of mana changed the balance of the world, Dongsoo couldn't beat Dongsuk.

Dongsoo congratulated his brother when he awakened as a C-Rank, but boiled with jealousy.

When his older brother discovered a "new way of making money" that could only be done with his powers and cut Dongsuk out of the deal, Dongsuk was furious. He followed his older brother, despite knowing that only awakened beings can safely enter a dungeon.

He survived- and realized that he had powers as well.

On the day he was evaluated as an S-Rank, with mana beyond what machines could measure, he clenched his fist with joy. For the first time in his life, he had surpassed Dongsuk.

SysConstStr.WebPolicy.SelectPickUp_Selec:
This is a function that increases your chance of drawing the SSRs on the Selection List. The Selection List can be changed at any time.

Draw Support
- An SSR is guaranteed to appear within 70 draws, and the count will reset upon acquisition.
- Starting with the 60th draw of the Draw Support, the draw rate of SSRs increases by 5.8% each time.
- When acquiring an SSR from the Draw Support, there is a 50% chance of acquiring one of the 3 SSRs on your Selection List, with equal odds of acquiring any particular one on the list, and a 50% chance of acquiring an SSR not on the list, divided equally among the other available items.
- If the SSR you obtain through Draw Support is not on your Selection List, there's a 1/3 chance you will obtain 1 of the 3 SSRs on your Selection List with your next Draw Support attempt.

Weapon Custom Draw
This increases the appearance rate of SSRs on your Selection List. The Selection List can be changed at any time.

Draw Support
- An SSR is guaranteed to appear within 70 draws. The count will reset when an SSR is acquired.
- Starting with the 60th Draw Support draw, the chance of an SSR appearing increases by 5.8% each draw.
- When acquiring an SSR from the Draw Support, there is a 50% chance you will acquire one of the 2 SSRs on your Selection List, with equal odds of acquiring any particular one on the list, and there is a 50% chance you will acquire one of the SSRs not on your Selection List, divided equally among the other available weapons.
- If the SSR you obtain through Draw Support is not the one on your Selection List, there's a 50% chance to obtain 1 of the 2 SSRs on your Selection List with your next Draw Support attempt.

Story.CharacterInfo_34:
Even before he became a Hunter, Min Byung-Gu couldn't turn away a person in need. People always used to tell him that he was almost too good to be true.

These words only added to the weight on his shoulders, but there wasn't anything he could do but carry on.

They were right, after all. He knew that he was a naturally kind person, and that was probably why he was Awakened with the rare and coveted power of Healing.

Maybe it was his calling.

Hunters, despite putting their lives on the line to protect their country and their people, often have no one to protect them as they fight against monsters.

Perhaps that's why he was given this power, so that he could use it to help the tired and battered Hunters as they risk their lives.

That was all the encouragement he needed to give it his all on the battlefield. He worked with a blazing passion, saving every Hunter he could, even if it meant throwing himself in harm's way.

Even as more Hunters switched from protecting others to pursuing profits, his conviction never wavered.

He could remain so stalwart in his approach because he had the strength to back it up. His exceptional abilities allowed him to walk his own path, and shrug off the expectations of others.

But, eventually, his conviction collided with the brick wall of reality. And he couldn't escape the collision.

When he saw the horde of ants that conquered Jeju Island, he realized that he could not protect everyone with his strength only, no matter how hard he tried.

After being dragged out by his surviving comrades and forced to abandon the bodies of the others, Min Byung-Gu's unwavering resolve sank under the weight of despair, never to be seen again.

Awake or asleep, his comrades' cries for help never left his mind, and no matter how hard he tried to think of how he could have handled it better, he arrived at the same conclusion: There was nothing he could have done.

He tried to drown his doubts with success and returned to the field. But the sight of the first Hunter getting wounded on his watch completely broke him. He came to the conclusion that he couldn't save everyone... or anyone. Despite Baek Yoonho's strong protests, he immediately announced his retirement.

Although he'd carried the weight of the world on his shoulders his entire life, he realized that the lives of his comrades were too much of a burden for him to handle. He knew he must put down the burden if he was to stop himself from breaking beneath it.

The power of Healing was not as omnipotent as he once thought, nor was he the incredibly capable person that everyone thought he was.

Those were the facts he came face to face with when the very first thought that came into his head when the ants swarmed was "I'm glad they're not after me."

He wasn't a savior, or even a kind person. He was just an ordinary person that lucked into a great power and fed off praise.

His long-held conviction was nothing more than a hollow justification of his unearned fame. That is how Min Byung-Gu fell apart.

Story.CharacterInfo_36:
Everything that happens in this world follows natural laws and can be explained with logic. The supernatural is but a myth, created by humans to explain things beyond their comprehension.

That's what Lee Bora always thought. She was firm in her belief that nothing in the world is unexplainable. Even if something inexplicable were to happen in front of her very eyes, she believed that it was only her lack of immediate understanding that left her without an explanation and that with time and knowledge, she'd be able to fully understand what had happened.

There was no time to waste on being bewildered by illusions or chasing phantoms. If you let even one ethereal problem into your life, it wouldn't be long before they took over. You need to be able to see the world for what it is.

She arrived at this conclusion when she was just a little girl, after seeing the twisted look on her grandmother's face as she talked about the incorporeal. She started doing her own research to explain everything "paranormal" with cold, hard facts.

Whenever she could find the explanation for something odd and confirmed that it matched to the tiniest detail, she felt her anxieties ease a little. Her grandmother had insisted that Bora become a medium, just like her. She was comforted that each explanation loosened her grandmother's vice grip on her future.

But the world had something else in store for her. All of the effort she put in to denying the paranormal went up in flames as the supernatural soon invaded every aspect of human life. And as salt in the wound, the world made her one of the people that were able to interact with these supernatural powers.

She might've wrapped her head around it if she was given the ability to strengthen her body to make some sort of physical attack, but the power she was given was a force beyond our current understanding of physics.

At times, she felt that the world as she knew it has ended, and that everything she stood for was a lie. But she wasn't the type of person to give up that easily. She wouldn't let her whole life be in vain.

So, she arrived at a new objective.

She had considered pretending that she didn't have the ability to feel mana and living out the rest of her life as a regular person. But that would mean admitting defeat and running away from the problem.

And that didn't sit right with her. Instead, she would rather run headfirst into the world of mana.

Through first-hand experience, and lots and lots of data, she could then arrive at a new truth, and claim victory over the supernatural once more.

She does happen to be using the charms that her grandmother made for her to fight, but that is but a minor setback.

She has embarked on a grand quest to disprove the supernatural and claim control of her life once more. Though dealing with her grandmother's smug face is incredibly frustrating- trivial though her grandma's self-righteousness may be.

It.StringStory.302030004:
[When the signal flare sounds in the silence of the night, use your mana power and swing your sword as if you're dancing. Be swift enough that only the trail of light remains.]

A wielding a sword is like running:

First, the fleeting moment of silence when all her nerves are focused: ears, eyes, and legs.

When the starting pistol finally fires, both of her legs move instinctively towards the goal, pumping with all their might.

Even when she holds a sword and faces a magic beast, she runs on instinct and never holds back, underscored by the sound of a signal flare that only her ears can hear.

When the now-familiar energy rises from deep within her heart, giving her strength...

Her sword cuts through the darkness like light itself.

1. At the start of the battle and during normal attack phases, Kamish's wings and tail are <color=#64E0F7>invulnerable</color> and cannot be attacked.

2. During battle, Kamish will attempt to <color=#BF9DFF>enhance its body parts</color> during certain attack phases. The parts being enhanced become <color=#FEBD21>vulnerable</color> and can be attacked.

3. Kamish's successfully <color=#BF9DFF>enhanced body parts</color> can only be countered with <color=#FF8741>Breaks</color> and <color=#FF8741>Elemental Accumulation</color>.

4. Destroying its wings puts Kamish into a <color=#92D050>regeneration state</color>, preventing Kamish from attacking with them.

5. Destroying its tail puts Kamish into a <color=#92D050>regeneration state</color>, preventing Kamish from attacking with it.

6. When both of Kamish's wings and tails are <color=#BF9DFF>enhanced</color>, Kamish uses Annihilation Descent, dealing massive damage to the entire team.

As his bewildered target started to question him, Taeshik drove a dagger into his target's body and watched them crumple.

"This is the perfect place for me," he thought, methodically twisting the knife in his fallen target.

When he left the gate, he blended into the crowd, hiding the possessions he'd swiped, including a shiny rock inscribed with a strange pattern.

Four years later, Taeshik's skills got him hired at the Hunters Association.

He gained respect for his eagerness to go out into the field, and no one questioned why the survival rate of his raids was so low.

Thus, he was able to continue his "hunter-hunting" habit... at least, until he ran into Sung Jinwoo.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc017:
Yoo Myunghan, chairman of Yoojin Construction, had three children. As the youngest of the three, Yoo Jinho could never measure up to his siblings.

His older brother Jinsung was a genius. He's never gotten less than first place in anything and led many of his father's projects to glowing praise. His older sister Jinhee was a beloved musical savant.

But Jinho did not share his siblings' talents. No matter how hard he tried to catch up, the result was always the same: his father's disappointment and his brother's condescending laughter.

Yoo Myunghan knew that his company had grown too swiftly to remain stable without constant vigilance. He wanted his company to go to his children, but also knew they needed to be capable of succeeding him.

Not only was Jinho mediocre in academics and art, he was a nervous wreck, despite Myunghan's efforts to raise him otherwise. Myunghan was especially strict in matters that concerned his youngest child.

The result was that Jinho was terrified of failure. He walked on eggshells in his own house to avoid his father's scolding, which only brought him greater scrutiny.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc014:
Every time he saw a character like him in popular culture, he would privately laugh to himself. They were all given some sort of tragic backstory or a web of complex motivations. He had no such motivations.

There was no special reason behind his cruelty. He was merely entertained by his victims' fearful cries as they hopelessly struggled in the face death.

Eventually, he would get bored of tormenting one particular sort of creature and would set out in search of others. He was always searching for a new victim, getting bored of them faster each time. As he ran out of stimuli, large swaths of time began to pass without holding any meaning to him.

He needed... something stronger.

And he knew what it was: the most dangerous prey. Humans.

This is a function that increases your chance of drawing SSRs on your Selection List.
The Selection List can be changed at any time.

Draw Support
- An SSR is guaranteed to appear within 70 draws, and the count will reset upon acquisition.
- Starting with the 60th draw of the Draw Support, the draw rate of the SSR increases by 5.8% each time.
- When acquiring an SSR from the Draw Support, there is a 50% chance of acquiring one of the 3 SSRs on your Selection List, with equal odds of acquiring any particular one on the list, and a 50% chance of acquiring an SSR not on the list, divided equally among the other available items.
- If the SSR you obtain through Draw Support is not on your Selection List, there's a 1/3 chance to obtain 1 of the 3 SSRs on the Selection List on your next Draw Support attempt.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc015:
He set out in search of a victim.

But when he finally closed in on his selected target, they were whisked away into a cerulean vortex, right before his very eyes.

He immediately thought of the "blue portals" he had heard about on the news.

Only the chosen could enter, and those who did not return swiftly were lost forever.

Curious, he took a tentative step forward. Their exclusivity had been greatly exaggerated: he easily slipped into the gate.

There, he saw his target fighting off a horde of monsters. Though his frightened target's movements were clumsy, the monsters were steadily decreasing in number.

It was only after the fight had ended that his target noticed he had arrived. Kang Taeshik put on his best "helpless civilian" act and approached.
Story.CharacterInfo_Desc009:
"Wait... that bridge looks like it's going to collapse."

The Guild was conducting a mock raid for newly admitted hunters at their training grounds. No real Magic Monsters were involved, of course. The hunters-in-training needed to safely find the way out of the mock-dungeon.

Park Heejin was torn about whether to tell the other newbies about the bridge.

The training grounds were faithfully modeled after the inside of a dungeon, and the hunters were faced with a shallow ravine. There was a sign warning them that it was meant to symbolize a much deeper fall, and there was a purposefully weathered bridge leading to the other side.

When her fellow hunters cautiously started to cross, Heejin noticed something give, ever so slightly. She refused to join them.

Story.CharacterInfo_Desc012:
By passing the test, she was given the opportunity to attend practical training and official raids, but had earned the ire of her angry teammates. There was nothing that she could really say.

How could she have explained her scarily correct premonition? She couldn't trust her own instincts, and they wouldn't have either.

The incident on that snowy mountain changed her mind. She was chased out of the Red Gate with her tail between her legs, unable to even retrieve the corpses of the people she'd been training with... If only she had trusted herself. She swore she would never let that happen again.
Story.CharacterInfo_Desc008:
He once again drifted from sport to sport, but he had a hard time finding that challenge. Life was boring, and none of the praise he received satisfied him anymore.

As life would have it, the greater challenge he was seeking finally arrived with the gates. He wasn't the strongest awakened being known to man, but he was capable of becoming an A-Rank Hunter.

Hunter training was beyond boring. He wanted to go on raids right away, but his guild talked him down and convinced him to follow due process.

They told him that once he learned the ropes, he would be leading raids himself. He would become famous, just like the S-Rank hunters.

All of it went straight to his head. He thought about Park Jongsoo, another A-Rank hunter who led his own major guild despite not being an S-Rank hunter. With his training complete and his dreams of glory dancing in his mind, Kim Chul entered the C-Rank gate for some practical combat training. Inside, however, all that was waiting for him were biting winds blowing over a snowy plain... and Ice Elves, better known by their moniker: "Ice Slayers".

It.StringStory.302030056: To Lee Joohee, light was meant to save lives. She knew a gruff old man who always insisted that a healer should never lead the charge, so her comrades remained by her side until the very end despite their fragile bodies. Because of them, her light was warm. Then, in the blink of an eye, the gate closed. When she came to, she found herself lying outside where the gate had been. No one believed her, but she insisted... "Everyone is waiting for me back inside the gate." So she chose to go alone. Though her spirit was wounded and broken, she gritted her teeth and pressed on. She never stopped, following wherever the light led. The Guide of the Blessed Light never has to search for the way. She simply shines of her own accord and illuminates the way to those she's destined to find. "Please wait for me. I promise I'll save everyone."
